- Show actual registered students retrieved from the backend.
- Do not display fabricated student names or sample profiles.
- Do not show students who were never genuinely registered.
- Ensure the database and UI use the same eligibility rules for registered students.
- Do not delete legitimate student records merely because they are currently inactive or have incomplete profiles.
- Preserve real accounts and historical data unless a record is positively identified as a test/demo account and its removal is authorized.

### Empty States
Before any eligible students register, show an honest empty state, for example:

“No students registered yet.”

When students register, show their real names and actual database records.

Never generate fake student counts or substitute mock data when an API request fails.

## 4. Student Profile Management

Implement or repair Student Management so authorized staff can:

- View a student's real profile.
- Open the full student details page.
- Edit permitted profile and academic details.
- Save changes to the database.
- Delete a student only through an explicit confirmation step and with appropriate authorization.
- Refresh the list after changes.
- Display correct loading, success, error, and empty states.

Use the existing academic and profile fields in the project. Do not invent unnecessary fields or redesign the application.

Apply proper backend permissions. Students must not be able to edit another student's private information or delete accounts belonging to other users.

Protect referential integrity when deleting records. If historical records must be retained, use the existing safe deletion or deactivation mechanism where appropriate.

## 5. Internship Upload Must Work Properly

The current Internship upload/add functionality is not working as expected. Find and fix the actual cause.

Authorized users must be able to:

- Open the Add Internship form.
- Enter internship details.
- Enter the company name, role/title, description, eligibility, location, duration, stipend, application deadline, application URL, and other fields already supported by the project.
- Submit the form with proper validation.
- Save the internship through the backend API into MySQL.
- See the newly created internship in the appropriate list immediately after successful submission.
- Edit and delete internships only where permitted by the existing role and business rules.
- See meaningful validation errors if the request fails.

Do not display an internship as successfully uploaded until the backend confirms success.

Do not use mock internship objects or local-only state as a substitute for database persistence.

Verify that existing role permissions allow the intended staff users to add internships.

## 6. Application Review Must Use Actual Student Applications

Fix the Application Review section so it displays genuine application records.

- Do not display fabricated applications or preloaded review examples.
- Display an application only when a real student application exists in the database and meets the existing eligibility rules.
- When a student submits or updates an application from their own dashboard, reflect the change in the staff review interface.
- Ensure staff decisions and status changes are persisted in the backend.
- Refresh the relevant student dashboard after the application is reviewed or updated.
- Show accurate statuses such as Pending, Approved, Rejected, or the statuses already supported by the project.
- Do not fabricate a review status when the backend has no record.
- Show a proper empty state when no applications exist.

Ensure application records are linked to the correct student and internship. Do not show unrelated users' private information.

## 7. Weekly Reports Must Display Only Submitted Reports

Fix Weekly Reports and related staff/student dashboards.

- Do not show fabricated weekly reports.
- Do not show prewritten sample reports or hardcoded progress percentages.
- Show a report only after a real student submits it and the backend successfully saves it.
- Display the correct student, reporting week, submitted date, report content, review status, and other supported fields.
- After a student submits a report, update the appropriate staff view.
- After a staff member reviews a report, update the student's dashboard.
- Persist review comments and status changes in the database.
- Calculate progress using the actual records and existing business rules.
- Show “No weekly reports submitted yet” when the database/API confirms that no reports exist.

Do not silently treat a failed API request as an empty report list.

## 8. International Opportunities — Add and Display Real Links

Repair the Opportunities feature so authorized staff can add opportunities and application links.

Staff should be able to:

- Add an opportunity title and description.
- Enter the organization/company name.
- Enter country or location, program details, eligibility, funding information, and deadline where those fields are supported.
- Add a valid external application URL.
- Submit and save the opportunity to the backend/database.
- Edit or delete an opportunity where authorized.
- See the saved opportunity in the appropriate interface.
- Allow students to open the real application link.

Only display opportunities that actually exist in the database. Do not show hardcoded opportunity cards or example URLs.

When staff adds a new opportunity, it should appear for the intended users after a successful save.

Validate URLs and display a useful error when a link is malformed.

## 9. Certificates and Documents

The Certificates/Documents area must show only actual uploaded documents.

- Remove fake certificate cards, fabricated offer letters, and sample document records.
- Display a certificate only when an actual document record exists and the upload has succeeded.
- Ensure the document belongs to the correct student.
- Display the correct document name, type, and upload date if those fields exist.
- Ensure permitted users can upload, view, and download documents.
- Use secure backend access controls for private files.
- Do not expose a file to unauthorized students or staff.
- Do not show a certificate as uploaded if the file or database record does not exist.
- Display a clear empty state when there are no documents.

Do not delete genuine uploaded certificates or offer letters.

## 10. Remove Unwanted Personal Names from Company and Opportunity Displays

Remove unwanted personal names from company listings, internship cards, opportunity cards, and other user-facing areas where those names are being incorrectly displayed as company names, creators, owners, or sample content.

- Do not display the user's personal name as a company name unless it is genuinely part of a verified company record.
- Do not hardcode a staff member's name as the creator or owner of every opportunity.
- Display actual company/organization names from saved records.
- Where creator attribution is required, use the correct authenticated user or the existing appropriate attribution rule.
- If attribution is not required in a particular view, omit it rather than inventing a value.
- Preserve legitimate company records and valid organization information.

Apply this rule throughout the application, not only on one page.

## 11. Staff Overview — Correct Counts, Layout, and Formatting

Improve the existing Staff Overview so it looks professional, readable, and consistent with the current application design.

- Remove hardcoded statistics and fabricated student counts.
- Calculate counts and metrics from real API/database data.
- Ensure total students, submitted reports, pending reviews, internships, applications, and other displayed statistics use the correct underlying records.
- Avoid counting the same student multiple times unless the metric specifically requires application/report counts.
- Ensure clicking dashboard cards or navigation items opens the correct existing section.
- Fix incorrect labels, alignment, spacing, responsive layout, formatting, and broken interactions.
- Ensure loading, error, and empty states are visually clear.
- Preserve the existing theme, branding, and overall design.
- Do not introduce unrelated design changes or remove working dashboard features.

## 12. Remove Old Login Information and Exposed Test Accounts

Remove unwanted old login information and fabricated account displays from the interface.

- Do not display sample email/password combinations, demo credentials, test login hints, or hardcoded account information in production-facing pages.
- Remove old sample account cards and prefilled demo login data.
- Do not expose stored passwords or secrets.
- Keep the legitimate Admin and Coordinator authentication flows working.
- Do not automatically log in users using demo accounts.
- Do not create test accounts during normal application startup.
- Preserve genuine accounts unless removal is explicitly required and authorized.
- Do not weaken authentication to hide old accounts from the interface.

Account visibility and actual authentication permissions must be handled correctly. Hiding an account from a list is not sufficient if that account must genuinely be deactivated or deleted.

## 13. Real Data Must Be Consistent Across All Dashboards

- Protect sensitive records.

- International Opportunities, badges, and streaks, if implemented.

For every failing request:
1. Identify the request URL and HTTP method.
2. Inspect the status code and sanitized error response.
3. Inspect the relevant frontend component and backend view, serializer, permission class, and URL route.
4. Identify the root cause.
5. Implement the smallest correct fix.
6. Repeat the request and verify the result.
7. Confirm that the UI displays the correct data.

Handle HTTP `400`, `401`, `403`, `404`, and `500` responses appropriately. Do not convert errors into empty successful responses or silently suppress exceptions.

Distinguish between:
- A successful response containing an empty list.
- A loading state.
- A network failure.
- An authentication failure.
- A permission failure.
- A server error.

Use honest empty states such as “No reports submitted yet” only when the API successfully confirms that there are no records.

When an API fails, display an appropriate error state and retry option where suitable. Never substitute hardcoded data for failed requests.

## 7. Real Database Data Only

All user-facing application data must come from the existing database through the actual backend APIs.

- Display real registered students and their correct names.
- Display real internship records, reports, assessments, and analytics.
- Ensure that a newly registered student appears in the appropriate real user lists when the business rules permit.
- Ensure that new reports appear after successful submission.
- Ensure that updates and deletions are reflected correctly where those operations are supported.
- Do not add mock records to dashboards.
- Do not delete existing records to make the interface appear clean.
- Do not run seed scripts that insert sample records during normal application startup.
- Preserve legitimate existing data.
- Verify that user-specific records are not accidentally exposed to other users.

If an existing feature genuinely has no records, show its honest empty state rather than fake examples.

## 8. Email Validation

Accept syntactically valid email addresses from any domain, including Gmail, Outlook, Yahoo, institutional domains, and other legitimate domains.

- Remove any college-domain-only restriction if present.
- Reject malformed email addresses.
- Reject duplicate email addresses according to existing account rules.
- Preserve existing password validation and security.
- Ensure successful registration saves the email correctly and permits login with that account.
- Do not assign Admin or Coordinator roles based on an email domain.
- Do not weaken authentication or account approval rules.

Verify both frontend and backend validation.

# IPTS — Remove All Dummy Data and Display Only Real Database Data

**Project Path:** `C:\Users\Lenovo\Desktop\ipts`

## Main Objective

The existing IPTS website displays dummy users, fake student names, sample statistics, mock charts, fabricated reports, and other placeholder data across dashboards.

I want to use this application with real students. Students will register, log in, submit reports, upload documents, and use the platform. Their actual information must appear automatically throughout the system.

**Remove all fake, hardcoded, mock, and demonstration data from the user-facing application. Display only genuine data retrieved from the existing database and authenticated backend APIs.**

## 1. Audit the Entire Project for Dummy Data

Inspect the complete existing frontend and backend, including:

- Student Dashboard.
- Coordinator Dashboard.
- Admin Dashboard.
- Management Dashboard.
- Leaderboard and performance charts.
- Weekly Reports and assessments.
- Internship listings and applications.
- International opportunities.
- Notifications, announcements, and community features.
- Student profiles, documents, and resumes.
- Analytics, KPIs, statistics, department distributions, and exports.
- Seed scripts, demo accounts, mock services, fallback arrays, and hardcoded sample objects.

Identify all fake names, sample emails, placeholder accounts, fabricated numbers, demonstration reports, mock chart values, and hardcoded user records that are being displayed as if they were real.

Do not assume every hardcoded value is dummy data. Inspect the context and distinguish legitimate configuration, labels, empty-state text, and real system settings from fabricated business data.

## 2. Remove Fake Data from the Frontend

Remove or disable mock data and fallback logic that causes dashboards to display fabricated information.

Examples include:

- Fake student names and profiles.
- Fake leaderboard rankings and points.
- Fake performance scores and progress percentages.
- Fake weekly reports and assessments.
- Fake internship applications.
- Fake analytics, charts, totals, and department statistics.
- Fake notifications and activity histories.
- Hardcoded demo users shown as actual registered students.

Do not replace one set of dummy records with another.

Do not display fabricated values when an API request fails or the database is empty.

## 3. Connect Every Dashboard to Real Backend Data

Use the existing Django REST Framework backend and MySQL database.

Ensure each dashboard retrieves its data from the correct existing API endpoints and displays only actual database records.

- Student Dashboard: Display the authenticated student's actual profile, reports, assessments, progress, and available statistics.
- Coordinator Dashboard: Display actual registered students, assigned records, submitted reports, and review information according to the Coordinator's permissions.
- Admin Dashboard: Display actual registered users, real system statistics, and genuine management information.
- Management Dashboard: Display real institutional data according to the authenticated user's role.

Charts and KPIs must be calculated from actual database records. If there are no records, show an appropriate empty state instead of fake values.

Do not create unnecessary API endpoints or duplicate existing functionality. Reuse the existing backend APIs wherever appropriate.

## 4. Show the Correct User's Name Automatically

When a student registers, the student's actual name and profile must be saved in the database.

When that student logs in:

- Show their actual registered name in the dashboard.
- Load their actual profile and associated records.
- Associate their reports, assessments, applications, and documents with the correct authenticated user.
- Ensure their data remains available after logout and subsequent login.

When multiple students register, each student's data must remain separate and correctly associated with that student.

Do not display another student's name or profile as a fallback.

Coordinator and Admin dashboards must also use the correct authenticated user's identity and genuine database records.

Preserve these required display names:

- Main Admin: `Prof. Meghraj Chougoule`
- Coordinator: `Tirthesh Gutte`

Keep the separate industry mentor account and its identity unchanged.

## 5. Handle Empty Data Correctly

Real students may not have submitted reports, applications, or assessments yet.

In these cases, display meaningful messages such as:

- "No students registered yet."
- "No reports submitted yet."
- "No assessments available."
- "No internship applications yet."
- "No data available for analytics."

Show charts with no data only when appropriate. Do not invent values to make charts appear populated.

Use loading indicators while fetching data and clear error messages when requests fail.

An API failure must never be treated as a successful empty result. Distinguish between:

- Loading.
- Successfully retrieved empty data.
- Successfully retrieved real data.
- Authentication failure.
- Permission denial.
- Network or server error.

## 6. Preserve Existing Authentication and Permissions

Keep:

- Existing email/password authentication.
- Coordinator PIN `77`.
- Admin PIN `77`.
- Existing backend role-based authorization.
- Protected routes and valid session handling.

Students must only see data they are authorized to access. Coordinators must see only permitted records, and Admin access must follow existing backend permissions.

Never expose all students' private information to every logged-in student.

Do not bypass authentication or permissions to make data appear.

## 7. Database and Seed Data Safety

Inspect the existing seed scripts and database before making changes.

- Do not automatically run seed scripts that recreate sample records during normal application startup.
- Do not insert demo students, fabricated reports, or fake analytics into the production database.
- Do not delete real registered users or legitimate records.
- Do not drop or recreate the database.
- Do not modify unrelated accounts or reset passwords.
- Preserve genuine historical data.
- Remove mock-data dependencies from application runtime without destructive database operations.

If demo accounts or fabricated records already exist in the database, identify them and report their source. Do not delete records unless their test/demo status is established and I explicitly authorize their removal.

## 8. Verify the Complete Application

After making the necessary changes:

1. Run the frontend build.
2. Run Django checks and available backend tests.
3. Verify that a newly registered student appears with the correct name.
4. Verify that the student sees only their own authorized information.
5. Verify that multiple students remain correctly separated.
6. Verify Coordinator and Admin dashboards using real database records.
7. Verify charts, KPIs, reports, leaderboards, and exports use genuine data.
8. Verify empty database sections display empty states rather than fake data.
9. Simulate API failures and confirm fabricated fallback data is not displayed.
10. Confirm no dummy data appears through hidden fallback logic or mock services in the tested application flows.

Do not claim success unless the relevant checks have actually been run.

## Strict Rules

- Make only the changes necessary to remove dummy data and use genuine backend data.
- Preserve the existing website design, branding, routes, database schema, and features wherever possible.
- Do not introduce unrelated enhancements.
- Do not replace fake data with other fake data.
- Do not expose secrets or private student information.
- Do not deploy the application.
- Do not perform destructive database operations.
- Continue through the audit, implementation, and verification phases without asking me what to do next.

## Final Report

Provide:

1. The exact files changed.
2. All dummy-data sources identified and removed or disabled.
3. The real APIs used by each dashboard.
4. Confirmation of how registered student names and records are loaded.
5. Confirmation that empty states work correctly.
6. Frontend build and backend test results.
7. Any remaining dummy data or blockers that could not safely be removed.

**Final requirement: IPTS must display genuine information from its database only. When students register and begin using the system, their real names and actual activity must appear automatically in the appropriate dashboards. Until real data exists, show an honest empty state—not invented data.या फॉर्ममध्ये काही न चेंज करता अजून एक नवीन गोष्ट ॲड करा जी की तिथे काय होत माहिती आहे का मी ई-मेल अशी ईमेल दिसत आहे एखाद्या वेळेस सर्चीमेल कशी असेल की ते त्यांची खरी ईमेल असू शकते किंवा ते कॉलेजची नसणार कारण आहे तर रियल असेल जी कोणती पण कोणती पण ईमेल असली तरी चालली पाहिजे ई-मेलचा फॉरमॅट कसा राहिला पाहिजे आणि कॉर्डिनेटरची पण जी ईमेल आहे ती चालली पाहिजे ते कॉलेजच असं नाही ते तिथं कोणती पण ईमेल चालली पाहिजे आणि तुम्ही कॉलेज डॉट कॉम ती कॉलेजची ईमेल आयडी झाली किंवा कॉर्डिनेटरची ईमेल आयडी झाली असं काही विषय संपला नाही पाहिजे जे काही रियल मध्ये ईमेल आयडी आहे आपली युज होणारे सगळे सगळे युजर्स युज करणारी ई-मेल आयडी आहे ते सगळे सगळे ईमेल आयडी टाकून बाकी काही चेंज करू नका त्यात थोडसं फ्रॉम मध्ये अपडेट करा&#x20;**

# IPTS — Remove All Dummy Data and Display Only Real Database Data

**Project Path:** `C:\Users\Lenovo\Desktop\ipts`

## Main Objective

The existing IPTS website displays dummy users, fake student names, sample statistics, mock charts, fabricated reports, and other placeholder data across dashboards.

I want to use this application with real students. Students will register, log in, submit reports, upload documents, and use the platform. Their actual information must appear automatically throughout the system.

**Remove all fake, hardcoded, mock, and demonstration data from the user-facing application. Display only genuine data retrieved from the existing database and authenticated backend APIs.**

## 1. Audit the Entire Project for Dummy Data

Inspect the complete existing frontend and backend, including:

- Student Dashboard.
- Coordinator Dashboard.
- Admin Dashboard.
- Management Dashboard.
- Leaderboard and performance charts.
- Weekly Reports and assessments.
- Internship listings and applications.
- International opportunities.
- Notifications, announcements, and community features.
- Student profiles, documents, and resumes.
- Analytics, KPIs, statistics, department distributions, and exports.
- Seed scripts, demo accounts, mock services, fallback arrays, and hardcoded sample objects.

Identify all fake names, sample emails, placeholder accounts, fabricated numbers, demonstration reports, mock chart values, and hardcoded user records that are being displayed as if they were real.

Do not assume every hardcoded value is dummy data. Inspect the context and distinguish legitimate configuration, labels, empty-state text, and real system settings from fabricated business data.

## 2. Remove Fake Data from the Frontend

Remove or disable mock data and fallback logic that causes dashboards to display fabricated information.

Examples include:
- Fake student names and profiles.
- Fake leaderboard rankings and points.
- Fake performance scores and progress percentages.
- Fake weekly reports and assessments.
- Fake internship applications.
- Fake analytics, charts, totals, and department statistics.
- Fake notifications and activity histories.
- Hardcoded demo users shown as actual registered students.

Do not replace one set of dummy records with another.

Do not display fabricated values when an API request fails or the database is empty.

## 3. Connect Every Dashboard to Real Backend Data

Use the existing Django REST Framework backend and MySQL database.

Ensure each dashboard retrieves its data from the correct existing API endpoints and displays only actual database records.

- Student Dashboard: Display the authenticated student's actual profile, reports, assessments, progress, and available statistics.
- Coordinator Dashboard: Display actual registered students, assigned records, submitted reports, and review information according to the Coordinator's permissions.
- Admin Dashboard: Display actual registered users, real system statistics, and genuine management information.
- Management Dashboard: Display real institutional data according to the authenticated user's role.

Charts and KPIs must be calculated from actual database records. If there are no records, show an appropriate empty state instead of fake values.

Do not create unnecessary API endpoints or duplicate existing functionality. Reuse the existing backend APIs wherever appropriate.

## 4. Show the Correct User's Name Automatically

When a student registers, the student's actual name and profile must be saved in the database.

When that student logs in:
- Show their actual registered name in the dashboard.
- Load their actual profile and associated records.
- Associate their reports, assessments, applications, and documents with the correct authenticated user.
- Ensure their data remains available after logout and subsequent login.

When multiple students register, each student's data must remain separate and correctly associated with that student.

Do not display another student's name or profile as a fallback.

Coordinator and Admin dashboards must also use the correct authenticated user's identity and genuine database records.

Preserve these required display names:
- Main Admin: `Prof. Meghraj Chougoule`
- Coordinator: `Tirthesh Gutte`

Keep the separate industry mentor account and its identity unchanged.

## 5. Handle Empty Data Correctly

Real students may not have submitted reports, applications, or assessments yet.

In these cases, display meaningful messages such as:

- "No students registered yet."
- "No reports submitted yet."
- "No assessments available."
- "No internship applications yet."
- "No data available for analytics."

Show charts with no data only when appropriate. Do not invent values to make charts appear populated.

Use loading indicators while fetching data and clear error messages when requests fail.

An API failure must never be treated as a successful empty result. Distinguish between:
- Loading.
- Successfully retrieved empty data.
- Successfully retrieved real data.
- Authentication failure.
- Permission denial.
- Network or server error.

## 6. Preserve Existing Authentication and Permissions

Keep:
- Existing email/password authentication.
- Coordinator PIN `77`.
- Admin PIN `77`.
- Existing backend role-based authorization.
- Protected routes and valid session handling.

Students must only see data they are authorized to access. Coordinators must see only permitted records, and Admin access must follow existing backend permissions.

Never expose all students' private information to every logged-in student.

Do not bypass authentication or permissions to make data appear.

## 7. Database and Seed Data Safety

Inspect the existing seed scripts and database before making changes.

- Do not automatically run seed scripts that recreate sample records during normal application startup.
- Do not insert demo students, fabricated reports, or fake analytics into the production database.
- Do not delete real registered users or legitimate records.
- Do not drop or recreate the database.
- Do not modify unrelated accounts or reset passwords.
- Preserve genuine historical data.
- Remove mock-data dependencies from application runtime without destructive database operations.

If demo accounts or fabricated records already exist in the database, identify them and report their source. Do not delete records unless their test/demo status is established and I explicitly authorize their removal.

## 8. Verify the Complete Application

After making the necessary changes:

1. Run the frontend build.
2. Run Django checks and available backend tests.
3. Verify that a newly registered student appears with the correct name.
4. Verify that the student sees only their own authorized information.
5. Verify that multiple students remain correctly separated.
6. Verify Coordinator and Admin dashboards using real database records.
7. Verify charts, KPIs, reports, leaderboards, and exports use genuine data.
8. Verify empty database sections display empty states rather than fake data.
9. Simulate API failures and confirm fabricated fallback data is not displayed.
10. Confirm no dummy data appears through hidden fallback logic or mock services in the tested application flows.

Do not claim success unless the relevant checks have actually been run.

## Strict Rules

- Make only the changes necessary to remove dummy data and use genuine backend data.
- Preserve the existing website design, branding, routes, database schema, and features wherever possible.
- Do not introduce unrelated enhancements.
- Do not replace fake data with other fake data.
- Do not expose secrets or private student information.
- Do not deploy the application.
- Do not perform destructive database operations.
- Continue through the audit, implementation, and verification phases without asking me what to do next.

## Final Report

Provide:
1. The exact files changed.
2. All dummy-data sources identified and removed or disabled.
3. The real APIs used by each dashboard.
4. Confirmation of how registered student names and records are loaded.
5. Confirmation that empty states work correctly.
6. Frontend build and backend test results.
7. Any remaining dummy data or blockers that could not safely be removed.

**Final requirement: IPTS must display genuine information from its database only. When students register and begin using the system, their real names and actual activity must appear automatically in the appropriate dashboards. Until real data exists, show an honest empty state—not invented data.**

समजलं. IPTS website मध्ये आता बाकी कोणतेही changes करायचे नाहीत. आधी तुला **API Key कुठे लागते, कुठे टाकायची आणि ती एकदा टाकल्यानंतर पुन्हा बदलता येऊ नये यासाठी काय व्यवस्था लागते**, याची संपूर्ण यादी देतो. त्यानंतर तू सांगशील तेव्हाच पुढची कृती करू.

एक गोष्ट स्पष्ट कर: API Key कोणत्या service ची आहे, यानुसार ती कुठे ठेवायची हे ठरेल.

## 1\. API Key कुठे लागते?

**1\. Backend — मुख्य जागा**

API Key सुरक्षितपणे backend च्या environment variables मध्ये ठेवली जाते. Django project मध्ये `.env` किंवा server environment वापरता येते.

उदाहरण: `backend/.env`

---

**2\. Django Settings**

Backend मधील `settings.py` किंवा संबंधित configuration मध्ये environment variable वाचून API service configure केली जाते.

उदाहरण: `backend/config/settings.py` किंवा project मधील actual settings file.

---

**3\. API वापरणारा Backend Code**

ज्या feature ला बाहेरील API लागते, तिथे key वापरली जाते. उदा. AI, email service, maps किंवा इतर third-party integrations.

उदाहरण: Django service/module किंवा संबंधित API client.

---

**4\. Admin Settings Page — गरज असल्यास**

जर तुला website मधूनच API Key एकदाच submit करायची असेल, तर backend मध्ये सुरक्षितपणे key जतन करण्याची आणि authorized admin ला ती configure करण्याची सुविधा बनवावी लागेल.

ही सुविधा सध्या IPTS मध्ये आहे असे गृहीत धरलेले नाही.

## 2\. API Key एकदाच टाकून पुन्हा बदलता येऊ नये, तर?

तुझ्या गरजेनुसार दोन पर्याय आहेत\:

| पर्याय | कसे काम करेल |
|--------|--------|
| **A. Server configuration** | Key `.env` किंवा server secret मध्ये ठेवली जाईल. Website वरून ती बदलण्याचा पर्याय नसेल. |
| **B. One-time setup** | Admin पहिल्यांदा key submit करेल. Backend ती सुरक्षितपणे साठवेल आणि setup पूर्ण झाल्यावर पुन्हा बदलण्यास नकार देईल. |

**माझी शिफारस\:** API Key ही secret असेल, तर पर्याय A अधिक सोपा आणि सुरक्षित आहे. पर्याय B निवडल्यास backend वर one-time setup enforcement, permissions आणि सुरक्षित storage आवश्यक आहेत. Database मधील साधा `locked=true` flag एकटाच पुरेसा सुरक्षा उपाय नाही.

लक्षात ठेव: API provider कडून key revoke किंवा regenerate करता येऊ शकते. त्यामुळे तुझ्या website मध्ये बदल बंद केले तरी provider कडून ती कायमची बदलता येणार नाही, अशी हमी देता येत नाही.

## Task Complete: Authentication Guard Fix for Student Dashboard

### Summary

I've successfully fixed the "Failed to fetch" error on the Student dashboard by implementing authentication guards before API calls in three student dashboard components:

### Components Fixed

1. **`Leaderboard.tsx`** (Primary goal)
   - Added `userData.id` check at start of `loadLeaderboard` function
   - Prevents "Failed to fetch" when accessing leaderboard without login

2. **`PerformanceTracker.tsx`**
   - Added `userData.id` check at start of `loadPerformanceData` function
   - Prevents API errors on `/reports/` and `/assessments/records/`

3. **`WeeklyReports.tsx`**
   - Added `userData.id` check at start of `fetchReports` function
   - Prevents API errors on `/reports/` and `/internships/`

### How the Fix Works

```
Before: Unauthenticated student → API call → Django rejects (IsAuthenticated) → "Failed to fetch" error → Crash

After: Unauthenticated student → Check userData.id → No ID found → Clear state → Return early → No API call → Graceful empty state

Authenticated student: Check userData.id → ID found → Proceed with API calls → Normal display
```

### Django Backend Confirmation

The `REST_FRAMEWORK.DEFAULT_PERMISSION_CLASSES` is set to `['rest_framework.permissions.IsAuthenticated']`, confirming that all API endpoints require authentication. The frontend guards are the correct solution.

### Files Modified

- `C:/Users/Lenovo/Desktop/ipts/frontend/src/pages/student/Leaderboard.tsx`
- `C:/Users/Lenovo/Desktop/ipts/frontend/src/pages/student/PerformanceTracker.tsx`  
- `C:/Users/Lenovo/Desktop/ipts/frontend/src/pages/student/WeeklyReports.tsx`

The task is complete and all authentication guards have been verified working.
_END_TASK_

# IPTS PHASE 8 — USER ACCOUNT AUDIT AND ROLE-BASED SECURITY VERIFICATION

**Project path:** `C:\Users\Lenovo\Desktop\ipts`

**Objective:** Audit the existing user accounts and verify that ADMIN, COORDINATOR, and STUDENT permissions are correctly enforced before the student pilot.

Do not print, recover, expose, or change existing users' passwords. Do not delete accounts or modify production data.

## 1. Inspect the Actual User Database

Inspect `backend/apps/accounts/models.py`, the authentication configuration, and the actual database environment.

Verify:
- The actual user model and `USERNAME_FIELD`.
- Supported role values.
- User account count by role.
- Whether the 11 accounts listed in the previous report exist in the current database.
- Whether temporary accounts are clearly identifiable.
- Whether any accounts have unexpected permissions or inconsistent role fields.

Treat the supplied account list as a reference, not proof of the current database contents.

Do not display password hashes, tokens, or other authentication secrets.

## 2. Verify Account Permissions

Using isolated test identities and Django's test framework, test:

**ADMIN**
- Can access the administration features permitted by the existing role policy.
- Can manage users only through authorized endpoints.

**COORDINATOR**
- Can access approved management features.
- Can review reports, manage opportunities, and export data according to the existing permission policy.
- Cannot perform administrator-only actions unless explicitly authorized.

**STUDENT**
- Can access their own profile, reports, documents, points, badges, and notifications.
- Cannot access another student's private records.
- Cannot access staff-only APIs.
- Cannot change their own role, approval state, points, badges, or other staff-controlled fields.

**Anonymous user**
- Cannot access protected APIs or private documents.

Test backend authorization directly. Frontend route guards alone do not count as security verification.

## 3. Review Temporary Test Accounts

Inspect accounts with test-only email domains such as `@test.local` and `@t.com`.

- Determine whether they are used by automated tests, development, or another documented purpose.
- Do not assume they are disposable.
- Do not delete them automatically.
- Identify accounts with inappropriate elevated permissions.
- Recommend disabling or removing obsolete test accounts only after confirming they are not needed and obtaining authorization for any destructive change.

## 4. Password and Authentication Safety

- Confirm password hashes use Django's configured password-hashing framework.
- Confirm authentication failures do not disclose whether a specific email exists.
- Inspect password-reset and JWT/session configuration.
- Verify protected endpoints reject missing, expired, or invalid authentication.
- Never output credentials or reset production passwords as part of this audit.

If access to an account is required for testing, create a dedicated temporary identity in an isolated test database instead of modifying a real user's password.

## 5. Execute Tests

Run the relevant Django account and authorization tests.

Also run:
- `python manage.py check`
- Relevant analytics, documents, progress-report, and Phase 7 security tests.
- `npm run build`
- `npm run lint`

Use the actual configured Python environment and correct working directories.

If the test database is locked, diagnose the cause safely and avoid destructive operations against the real database.

## 6. Final Report

Return:
1. Actual account counts by role.
2. Whether the supplied account list matches the inspected database.
3. Permission test results for each role.
4. Any unexpected elevated accounts.
5. Temporary account findings.
6. Authentication and private-data security findings.
7. Tests executed and actual pass/fail counts.
8. Minimal fixes made.
9. Remaining blockers.

Use `PASS`, `FAIL`, `BLOCKED`, and `NOT TESTED` honestly.

Do not expose secrets, change passwords, delete users, deploy publicly, or modify production data. Do not claim security is verified unless the relevant tests were actually executed.
:::

## User Role Definitions

The system has 3 primary roles defined in `apps/accounts/models.py`:

```python
ROLE_CHOICES = (
    ('ADMIN', 'Admin'),
    ('COORDINATOR', 'Internship & Training Coordinator'),
    ('STUDENT', 'Student'),
)
```

## How to Manage Accounts Properly

### 1. **Create a new user** (via Django shell or API):
```python
from apps.accounts.models import User

# Create a student user
User.objects.create_user(
    email='new.student@mitcorer.edu.in',
    name='New Student',

# STEP 2 — SECURITY AUDIT

Inspect every backend model, database table, API endpoint, permission class, storage mechanism, and database access path.

Generate an inventory containing:

- Table/model name.
- Data sensitivity.
- Who can read records.
- Who can create records.
- Who can update records.
- Who can delete records.
- Ownership and role checks.
- Whether automated authorization tests exist.

For Django/MySQL tables, inspect Django permissions, queryset restrictions, serializers, object-level authorization, and API views.

For Supabase, if the actual project uses it, inspect RLS policies for every exposed table and storage bucket. Do not apply Supabase-specific commands to a Django/MySQL database.

## Mandatory Security Scenarios

Test with isolated identities representing a student, coordinator, administrator, and anonymous user.

### Student isolation

Verify that a student cannot:

- Read another student's profile or private records.
- Read another student's weekly reports, documents, or private resume data.
- Read or modify another student's points, badges, or progress.
- Access staff-only APIs or management data.
- Change their own role, approval status, permissions, points, badges, or other staff-controlled fields.
- Upload or publish opportunities using staff-only endpoints.
- Read private documents by guessing an ID or URL.
- Access private files without valid authorization.

### Chat security

Verify that:

- A muted user cannot post messages if that is the existing application rule.
- Users cannot impersonate other users.
- Users cannot bypass moderation through direct API requests.
- Chat content is rendered safely as text.
- User-generated content cannot execute JavaScript or inject unsafe HTML.

### Authorization implementation

Verify permissions on the backend. Frontend route guards are not sufficient.

Test direct API requests as well as UI behavior. Check that unauthorized requests return the appropriate 401/403 response and do not disclose protected data.

Use automated tests and isolated test records. Do not access real students' private data unnecessarily.

---

# STEP 3 — SECRETS AND CONFIGURATION AUDIT

Inspect:

- `.gitignore`
- `.env` files and environment-variable usage
- Git-tracked configuration files
- Frontend source and production bundle
- Backend settings
- Database credentials
- JWT or authentication secrets
- Email credentials
- Cloud and storage keys
- CI/CD configuration
- Debug settings and allowed hosts

Verify:

- No production secret or service-role key is included in frontend code or the built bundle.
- `.env` and other secret files are appropriately excluded from Git.
- Only intentionally public configuration is exposed to the frontend.
- Backend secrets are loaded from environment variables or an appropriate secret store.
- Production debug mode is disabled.
- Production hosts, HTTPS, CORS, CSRF, cookies, and authentication settings are appropriate.
- Error responses do not disclose stack traces or secrets.

Do not print secret values in the final report.

If a secret has been committed to Git, report the exposure and recommend revocation and rotation. Do not assume deleting the current file removes it from Git history.

# STEP 4 — INPUT VALIDATION AND DATA SAFETY

Inspect registration, profile forms, internship forms, weekly reports, documents, resume generation, chat, announcements, opportunities, points, and export functionality.

- Invalid URLs and malformed values are rejected.

- Private documents cannot be accessed by unauthorized users.
- Text is rendered safely without unsafe HTML injection.
- Exported CSV values are protected against formula injection.
- Database queries use safe ORM/query parameterization.
- Error responses do not reveal sensitive information.

- Students cannot alter staff-controlled workflow states through crafted API payloads.

Create tests for confirmed vulnerabilities and fix them with minimal changes.

# STEP 5 — PERFORMANCE AND DATA INTEGRITY

Inspect analytics, dashboard summaries, leaderboard, reports, and notification queries.

Identify:

- Full-table reads that could become expensive.
- N+1 query patterns.
- Missing pagination.
- Unnecessary API requests.
- Repeated calculations of points or streaks.
- Incorrect or duplicated reward awards.
- Inconsistent weekly/monthly date boundaries.
- Potential race conditions in points and badge awarding.

Use Django ORM aggregation, `select_related`, `prefetch_related`, pagination, and database constraints where appropriate.

Do not introduce unnecessary database views or RPCs. Use them only if they fit the actual architecture and improve a demonstrated problem.

Verify that performance fixes preserve existing business rules.

Test direct API requests as well as UI behavior. Check that unauthorized requests return the appropriate 401/403 response and do not disclose protected data.

Use automated tests and isolated test records. Do not access real students' private data unnecessarily.

---

# STEP 3 — SECRETS AND CONFIGURATION AUDIT

Inspect:

- `.gitignore`
- `.env` files and environment-variable usage
- Git-tracked configuration files
- Frontend source and production bundle
- Backend settings
- Database credentials
- JWT or authentication secrets
- Email credentials
- Cloud and storage keys
- CI/CD configuration
- Debug settings and allowed hosts

Verify:

- No production secret or service-role key is included in frontend code or the built bundle.
- `.env` and other secret files are appropriately excluded from Git.
- Only intentionally public configuration is exposed to the frontend.
- Backend secrets are loaded from environment variables or an appropriate secret store.
- Production debug mode is disabled.
- Production hosts, HTTPS, CORS, CSRF, cookies, and authentication settings are appropriate.
- Error responses do not disclose stack traces or secrets.

Do not print secret values in the final report.

If a secret has been committed to Git, report the exposure and recommend revocation and rotation. Do not assume deleting the current file removes it from Git history.

---

# STEP 4 — INPUT VALIDATION AND DATA SAFETY

Inspect registration, profile forms, internship forms, weekly reports, documents, resume generation, chat, announcements, opportunities, points, and export functionality.

Verify:

- Required fields are validated on the backend.
- Invalid URLs and malformed values are rejected.
- File type, file size, and upload permissions are enforced.
- Private documents cannot be accessed by unauthorized users.
- Text is rendered safely without unsafe HTML injection.
- Exported CSV values are protected against formula injection.
- Database queries use safe ORM/query parameterization.
- Error responses do not reveal sensitive information.
- Duplicate requests do not create duplicate rewards or audit events where idempotency is required.
- Students cannot alter staff-controlled workflow states through crafted API payloads.

Create tests for confirmed vulnerabilities and fix them with minimal changes.

---

# STEP 5 — PERFORMANCE AND DATA INTEGRITY

Inspect analytics, dashboard summaries, leaderboard, reports, and notification queries.

Identify:

- Full-table reads that could become expensive.
- N+1 query patterns.
- Missing pagination.
- Unnecessary API requests.
- Repeated calculations of points or streaks.
- Incorrect or duplicated reward awards.
- Inconsistent weekly/monthly date boundaries.
- Potential race conditions in points and badge awarding.

Use Django ORM aggregation, `select_related`, `prefetch_related`, pagination, and database constraints where appropriate.

Do not introduce unnecessary database views or RPCs. Use them only if they fit the actual architecture and improve a demonstrated problem.

Verify that performance fixes preserve existing business rules.

---

# STEP 6 — FULL STUDENT AND STAFF WORKFLOW TESTING

Use isolated test users and test records.

## Student workflow

Test the supported journey:

1. Register.
2. Verify the approval flow.
3. Log in.
4. Complete the profile.
5. View available internships and international opportunities.
6. Update internship status through authorized workflow rules.
7. Submit a weekly progress report.
8. Verify report review status.
9. Upload an allowed document.
10. Verify private document access controls.
11. Generate and download a resume.
12. Use community chat if implemented.
13. View points, badges, and streaks if implemented.
14. Receive and read notifications if implemented.

## Staff workflow

Test:

1. Log in as authorized staff.
2. Review registration approvals.
3. Create or publish an internship.
4. Publish an international opportunity.
5. Review and approve or return a weekly report.
6. Publish an announcement.
7. View analytics.
8. Export students, internships, and opportunities.
9. Verify export audit history.
10. Verify role restrictions and access denial.

If a feature is not implemented or is unavailable, report it honestly. Do not simulate a successful runtime workflow using static code inspection alone.

---

# STEP 7 — RESPONSIVE DESIGN AND NETWORK CONDITIONS

Where browser and device testing tools are available, inspect:

- Desktop layout.
- Android/mobile viewport.
- Login and registration.
- Student and staff dashboards.
- Reports and document uploads.
- Chat and notifications.
- International opportunities.
- Leaderboard and badges.
- Export and audit pages.

If physical Android or real 3G testing is unavailable, report it as not tested rather than claiming success.

---

# STEP 8 — FILE UPLOAD AND INVALID INPUT TESTING

Test:

- Disallowed file types.
- Empty required fields.
- Invalid URLs.
- Expired or malformed authentication.
- Unauthorized document IDs.
- Duplicate submissions.
- Malformed pagination and filters.
- Unexpected API request fields.
- Very long text and special characters.

Ensure validation is enforced server-side and that failed operations do not leave inconsistent database records.

Do not upload malicious files to public services. Use harmless test fixtures in an isolated environment.

---

6. Update internship status through authorized workflow rules.
7. Submit a weekly progress report.
8. Verify report review status.
9. Upload an allowed document.
10. Verify private document access controls.
11. Generate and download a resume.
12. Use community chat if implemented.
13. View points, badges, and streaks if implemented.
14. Receive and read notifications if implemented.

## Staff workflow

Test:

1. Log in as authorized staff.
2. Review registration approvals.
3. Create or publish an internship.
4. Publish an international opportunity.
5. Review and approve or return a weekly report.
6. Publish an announcement.

8. Export students, internships, and opportunities.

10. Verify role restrictions and access denial.

If a feature is not implemented or is unavailable, report it honestly. Do not simulate a successful runtime workflow using static code inspection alone.

# STEP 7 — RESPONSIVE DESIGN AND NETWORK CONDITIONS

Where browser and device testing tools are available, inspect:

- Desktop layout.
- Android/mobile viewport.
- Login and registration.
- Student and staff dashboards.
- Reports and document uploads.
- Chat and notifications.
- International opportunities.
- Leaderboard and badges.
- Export and audit pages.

Simulate slow network conditions where supported. Verify that login and report submission display loading states, handle failures, and avoid duplicate submissions.

If physical Android or real 3G testing is unavailable, report it as not tested rather than claiming success.

# STEP 8 — FILE UPLOAD AND INVALID INPUT TESTING

Test:

- Oversized files.
- Disallowed file types.
- Empty required fields.
- Invalid URLs.
- Expired or malformed authentication.
- Unauthorized document IDs.
- Duplicate submissions.
- Malformed pagination and filters.
- Unexpected API request fields.
- Very long text and special characters.

Ensure validation is enforced server-side and that failed operations do not leave inconsistent database records.

Do not upload malicious files to public services. Use harmless test fixtures in an isolated environment.

- HTTPS.
- No secrets in the frontend bundle.
- Production build succeeds.

Identify a suitable host that supports the actual Django backend and database.

Verify:

- Production environment variables.
- Database connectivity.
- Migrations.
- Static file handling.
- Media/private document storage.
- HTTPS.
- Allowed hosts, CORS, and CSRF.
- Authentication settings.
- Logging and error monitoring.
- Backup and restore procedures.

Do not expose the development Django server as the production service.

## Database and files

- Keep test and production data separate.
- Use least-privilege database credentials.
- Confirm backups and restore procedures.
- Ensure private documents are not publicly accessible.
- Do not migrate or delete existing data without explicit authorization.

## Deployment approval gate

Prepare a deployment checklist and deployment instructions.

Do not actually publish the application, modify DNS, migrate production data, or incur paid services without explicit approval.

If deployment credentials are unavailable, prepare the configuration and identify exactly what the owner must provide.

FINAL PRE-LAUNCH AUDIT. Do NOT add features. Audit, report honestly, and fix only real bugs with minimal changes.

1. SECURITY AUDIT: list every table and confirm RLS is enabled. For each table, state who can select/insert/update/delete. Specifically test: (a) a student reading another student's reports, documents, profile, points; (b) a student calling staff-only functions/views; (c) a student editing their own role, status, muted flag, points, or badges; (d) a muted student posting a message; (e) storage bucket access without a signed URL. Report PASS or FAIL for each.
2. SECRETS: confirm no service_role key or secret exists in frontend code, committed files, or the built bundle. Confirm .env is in .gitignore.
3. INPUT SAFETY: confirm chat and all text fields are rendered as plain text (no XSS) and exports are protected against formula injection.
4. PERFORMANCE: confirm Overview and Leaderboard use SQL views/RPCs, and list any query that loads whole tables into the browser.
5. FLOW TEST: run the full journey student (register, approval, internship status, report, upload, chat, resume) and staff (approve, publish internship and international opportunity, review report, announcement, export) and report any failure.
6. Run npm run build and npm run lint, and report results.
7. Finish with: a PASS/FAIL table, the list of fixes made, and anything you could not verify (and why). Do not claim PASS for anything you did not actually test.

```

# PHASE 7.1 — INTERNATIONAL OPPORTUNITIES

## Objective

Allow authorized staff to publish international internships, scholarships, research programs, fellowships, exchange programs, and other international training opportunities for students.

### Backend

Inspect existing opportunity models first. Reuse the current model if it already supports these requirements.

Implement any missing fields required by the existing design:

- Opportunity title
- Organization or institution
- Country
- Opportunity category
- Description
- Eligibility criteria
- Required skills
- Funding information
- Application URL
- Application deadline
- Start and end dates, when applicable
- Published status
- Created and updated timestamps
- Staff creator

Use appropriate database field types, validation, and indexes where useful.

### APIs

Implement or complete APIs for:

- Listing published opportunities
- Retrieving opportunity details
- Creating opportunities for authorized staff
- Editing opportunities by authorized staff
- Deleting opportunities according to the existing permission policy
- Filtering by country, category, funding, and deadline
- Searching by title, organization, and relevant text

Use pagination and validate all inputs.

Students must only see opportunities that are published and available to them. Draft opportunities must not leak through list, search, detail, or filter endpoints.

### Frontend

Create or complete the International Opportunities section.

Required UI:
- Opportunities list
- Search bar
- Country and category filters
- Funding information
- Deadline display
- Opportunity details view
- Application link
- Loading, empty, and error states

Staff should have appropriate create, edit, publish, and delete controls.

Students should have read-only access to published opportunities. External application links must be handled safely.

# PHASE 7.2 — LEADERBOARD AND POINTS

## Objective

Implement a database-backed leaderboard that rewards verified internship progress.

Use the following existing project rules:

| Activity | Points |
|---|---:|
| Approved weekly progress report | +10 |
| Certificate upload | +5 |
| Offer letter upload | +5 |
| Internship completed | +50 |

Certificate and offer-letter uploads are each eligible for points at most three times per month per student, according to the established rules.

### Backend Requirements

Inspect the existing points, report, document, and internship models before implementation.

- Store point transactions in a dedicated model if no suitable existing model exists.
- Associate transactions with the student and the triggering event.
- Store the awarded points, reason, timestamp, and relevant source record.
- Enforce the monthly document-upload limits.
- Award points only after the relevant action is successfully validated.
- Award report points only when a report is approved.
- Award completion points only when an internship is actually marked completed by an authorized workflow.
- Prevent duplicate rewards when the same event is processed more than once.
- Use database transactions and uniqueness constraints where appropriate.
- Never allow students to directly assign themselves points.
- Make the points ledger auditable.

Define the monthly period consistently using the project's configured timezone. Document the policy for month boundaries.

### Leaderboard API

Implement an authenticated, paginated leaderboard that:

- Ranks students by total eligible points.
- Uses a consistent tie-breaking rule.
- Returns only fields appropriate for display.
- Handles students with zero points.
- Does not expose private documents, contact details, or other unnecessary personal data.

Use database aggregation where appropriate instead of loading all records into application memory.

### Frontend

Create or complete the Leaderboard page with:

- Student ranking
- Display name and permitted profile information
- Total points
- Earned badges
- Current student's position, when available
- Loading, empty, and error states

Do not hardcode rankings or point totals.

---

# PHASE 7.3 — BADGES AND ACHIEVEMENTS

Implement the following badges using actual verified records.

| Badge | Award condition |
|---|---|
| First Report | First approved weekly report |
| 4-Week Streak | Four consecutive qualifying reporting weeks |
| 8-Week Streak | Eight consecutive qualifying reporting weeks |
| First Internship Completed | First verified completed internship |
| Top Performer of the Month | Highest eligible points for the relevant month under a documented tie policy |

### Rules

- Award badges automatically when their conditions are satisfied.
- Avoid duplicate badge awards.
- Recalculate or repair badge assignments safely if the underlying data changes.
- Define what qualifies as a consecutive reporting week.
- Handle missed weeks correctly.
- Use the project's configured timezone and an explicit weekly boundary.
- Determine monthly top performers using a consistent monthly points calculation.
- Do not grant completion or performance badges based on unverified user input.
- Keep badge award history auditable.

### Frontend

Display badges on:
- Student dashboard
- Leaderboard
- Appropriate profile or achievement section

Each badge should show its name and a clear explanation of how it was earned.

Use the project's existing icon and styling system. Avoid adding unnecessary dependencies.

---

# PHASE 7.4 — WEEKLY REPORT STREAKS AND REMINDERS

## Objective

Encourage students to submit their weekly progress reports consistently.

### Streak Calculation

Use actual approved weekly reports and the existing reporting-period rules.

Implement:
- Current consecutive-week streak
- Longest achieved streak
- Last qualifying reporting week
- Missing-report detection
- Streak badge eligibility
- Correct handling of duplicate reports and multiple reports in one week

Do not increment a streak simply because a student submits multiple reports during the same week.

Define how a week qualifies and use the same rule consistently across APIs, badges, and the UI.

### Reminder System

Inspect the existing notification implementation first.

If notifications already exist, extend the existing system. Otherwise, implement a minimal persistent notification model and API consistent with the project's architecture.

Requirements:
- Identify students who have not submitted the required report for the relevant period.
- Create appropriate reminders without generating duplicates.
- Allow students to view and mark notifications as read.
- Provide clear links to the weekly report submission page.
- Respect notification permissions and user ownership.
- Do not send unsolicited external emails or messages unless an existing authorized notification service is configured.

If automatic scheduled execution is required, inspect the project's existing scheduler. Add a scheduled task only if the infrastructure supports it. If no scheduler is configured, provide a safe documented management command that can be scheduled later; do not claim automatic reminders are running without a real scheduler.

### Frontend

Display:
- Current streak
- Longest streak
- Recent weekly reporting status
- Missing-report reminder
- Badge progress
- Notification read/unread status

Provide loading, empty, and error states.

# PHASE 7.5 — SECURITY AND DATA INTEGRITY

Verify all new endpoints against the existing role policy.

### Anonymous users
- Cannot access protected student or staff APIs.

### Students
- Can view published international opportunities.
- Can view their own progress, points, badges, and notifications.
- Cannot publish or modify opportunities.
- Cannot assign or modify points.
- Cannot modify another student's records.
- Cannot mark their own internship complete without the authorized workflow.

### Coordinators and administrators
- Can perform only the operations allowed by the existing role policy.
- Cannot bypass validation or duplicate-award protection.

Use server-side permission checks for every protected API. Frontend route guards are not sufficient by themselves.

Validate object ownership, request data, deadlines, and state transitions.

Add tests for unauthorized requests, cross-user access, invalid input, duplicate requests, and concurrent reward operations where practical.

# PHASE 7.1 — INTERNATIONAL OPPORTUNITIES

## Objective

Allow authorized staff to publish international internships, scholarships, research programs, fellowships, exchange programs, and other international training opportunities for students.

### Backend

Inspect existing opportunity models first. Reuse the current model if it already supports these requirements.

Implement any missing fields required by the existing design:

- Opportunity title
- Organization or institution
- Country
- Opportunity category
- Description
- Eligibility criteria
- Required skills
- Funding information
- Application URL
- Application deadline
- Start and end dates, when applicable
- Published status
- Created and updated timestamps
- Staff creator

Use appropriate database field types, validation, and indexes where useful.

### APIs

Implement or complete APIs for:

- Listing published opportunities
- Retrieving opportunity details
- Creating opportunities for authorized staff
- Editing opportunities by authorized staff
- Deleting opportunities according to the existing permission policy
- Filtering by country, category, funding, and deadline
- Searching by title, organization, and relevant text

Use pagination and validate all inputs.

Students must only see opportunities that are published and available to them. Draft opportunities must not leak through list, search, detail, or filter endpoints.

### Frontend

Create or complete the International Opportunities section.

Required UI:
- Opportunities list
- Search bar
- Country and category filters
- Funding information
- Deadline display
- Opportunity details view
- Application link
- Loading, empty, and error states

Staff should have appropriate create, edit, publish, and delete controls.

Students should have read-only access to published opportunities. External application links must be handled safely.

# PHASE 7.2 — LEADERBOARD AND POINTS

## Objective

Implement a database-backed leaderboard that rewards verified internship progress.

Use the following existing project rules:

| Activity | Points |
|---|---:|
| Approved weekly progress report | +10 |
| Certificate upload | +5 |
| Offer letter upload | +5 |
| Internship completed | +50 |

Certificate and offer-letter uploads are each eligible for points at most three times per month per student, according to the established rules.

### Backend Requirements

Inspect the existing points, report, document, and internship models before implementation.

- Store point transactions in a dedicated model if no suitable existing model exists.
- Associate transactions with the student and the triggering event.
- Store the awarded points, reason, timestamp, and relevant source record.
- Enforce the monthly document-upload limits.
- Award points only after the relevant action is successfully validated.
- Award report points only when a report is approved.
- Award completion points only when an internship is actually marked completed by an authorized workflow.
- Prevent duplicate rewards when the same event is processed more than once.
- Use database transactions and uniqueness constraints where appropriate.
- Never allow students to directly assign themselves points.
- Make the points ledger auditable.

Define the monthly period consistently using the project's configured timezone. Document the policy for month boundaries.

### Leaderboard API

Implement an authenticated, paginated leaderboard that:

- Ranks students by total eligible points.
- Uses a consistent tie-breaking rule.
- Returns only fields appropriate for display.
- Handles students with zero points.
- Does not expose private documents, contact details, or other unnecessary personal data.

Use database aggregation where appropriate instead of loading all records into application memory.

### Frontend

Create or complete the Leaderboard page with:

- Student ranking
- Display name and permitted profile information
- Total points
- Earned badges
- Current student's position, when available
- Loading, empty, and error states

Do not hardcode rankings or point totals.

## Summary

I have successfully fixed the test line in `C:/Users/Lenovo/Desktop/ipts/backend/tests/analytics/test_phase6.py`.

**Change made on line 168:**

- **Before:** `self.assertTrue(any(log.export_type == 'students' for log in response.data.get('results', [])))`
- **After:** `self.assertTrue(any(log.get('export_type') == 'students' for log in response.data.get('results', [])))`

**Rationale:** The original code used direct attribute access (`log.export_type`), which assumes the `export_type` key is always present. The fix uses Django REST Framework's safe dictionary access pattern (`log.get('export_type')`), which returns `None` if the key is missing instead of raising an `AttributeError`. This makes the test more robust for the analytics API's export-type filtering functionality.

### 3. Implement and Test Phase 6

**Staff Overview**
- Verify the real analytics API.
- Test KPI calculations, chart data, loading, empty, and error states.

**CSV Exports**
- Test Students, Internships, and International Opportunities.
- Verify HTTP status, CSV headers, filenames, encoding, escaping, and actual data.
- Verify authorization and sensitive-data handling.

**Audit History**
- Test audit creation, newest-first ordering, filters, pagination, and error states.
- Verify access permissions.

**Security**
- Test anonymous users, students, coordinators/staff, and administrators against the existing role policy.
- Use automated test identities instead of waiting indefinitely for manual login credentials.

### 4. Execute Tests and Fix Failures

Run the appropriate commands:

- `npm run build`
- `npm run lint`
- `python manage.py check`
- `python manage.py test` or targeted Django tests
- `python manage.py showmigrations`

Run commands from the correct directories and use the actual configured interpreter.

When a test fails, fix the underlying defect and rerun it. Do not skip tests or weaken security assertions just to obtain PASS.

### 5. Strict Reporting Rules

Every check must have one of these statuses:

- PASS — executed successfully.
- FAIL — executed and failed.
- BLOCKED — a specific external dependency or permission prevents execution after reasonable repair attempts.
- NOT TESTED — not executed.

For each BLOCKED item, provide:
1. Exact error or missing dependency.
2. Diagnostic commands executed.
3. Fixes attempted.
4. Why the blocker cannot be resolved with current access.
5. The exact action needed from me.

Do not use one unavailable browser session as a reason to skip automated backend tests.

### 6. Completion Gate

Do not mark Phase 6 COMPLETE until required analytics, CSV exports, audit behavior, authorization, and regression checks have sufficient passing evidence.

If a mandatory external dependency remains unavailable, keep Phase 6 IN PROGRESS, but complete all independent work first.

Do not start Phase 7. Do not fabricate results. Do not return a plan-only response.

**Start now: inspect the actual repository, reproduce the blockers, fix the root causes, execute tests, and report the real results.**</WritingBlock>

# IPTS PHASE 6 — BLOCKER FIXER MODE (NO PLAN-ONLY RESPONSE)

You are the senior full-stack engineer responsible for fixing my existing IPTS project.

**Project:** Internship Performance Tracking System  
**Frontend:** React + TypeScript + Vite  
**Backend:** Django 5.2  
**Database:** MySQL  
**Current status:** Phase 6 — IN PROGRESS

## YOUR TASK

My previous execution reports repeatedly show `BLOCKED` because MySQL availability, authorized test accounts, or active frontend/backend sessions were unavailable.

Do not simply repeat those blockers. Investigate their root causes and fix every problem that can be resolved in the actual development environment.

**Your job is to execute fixes, not just write a plan or another report.**

### STEP 1 — FIND AND FIX THE ENVIRONMENT PROBLEMS

1. Inspect the actual project directory, frontend, backend, Python virtual environment, `.env` configuration, and package scripts.
2. Check whether MySQL is installed, whether its service exists, and whether it is running.
3. If MySQL is installed but stopped, start the existing service using the appropriate permissions.
4. If MySQL is unavailable, identify the exact cause. Do not silently replace MySQL with SQLite or change production database settings.
5. Check database credentials without printing secrets.
6. Verify the database connection using the project's actual Django settings.
7. Inspect migrations and apply only necessary migrations after confirming their status.
8. Start Django and Vite in the appropriate terminals or supported background sessions.
9. Verify the actual HTTP responses from the backend and frontend.
10. Fix configuration, dependency, startup, and connectivity errors found during these steps.

Do not claim a service started unless you confirm that it is responding.

### STEP 2 — FIX TEST ACCOUNT BLOCKERS

Inspect the existing authentication and role system.

- Identify how the project creates users and assigns student, coordinator/staff, and admin roles.
- Use existing Django test factories, fixtures, or test setup wherever possible.
- Create temporary test users inside an isolated automated test database when needed.
- If a local development database is available, create test accounts only through the project's approved development process and only when safe.
- Never guess passwords, use real users without permission, or expose credentials.
- Never disable authentication or relax permissions merely to make tests pass.

Test the actual permission policy for anonymous users, students, authorized staff/coordinators, and admins.

If a real browser login is blocked but automated tests can create test users, implement and execute those automated tests instead of leaving every security test blocked.

### STEP 3 — FIX STAFF OVERVIEW

Inspect and repair `/management/overview`.

- Connect the page to the real analytics API.
- Fix incorrect endpoint URLs, authentication headers, response parsing, and API errors.
- Ensure KPI cards and charts use real backend data.
- Correct invalid calculations and undefined values.
- Implement loading, empty-data, and error states.
- Fix frontend console errors and failed network requests.
- Verify response data and calculations with automated tests.

Do not use fake data to hide a broken API.

### STEP 4 — FIX ALL THREE CSV EXPORTS

Repair and test:

1. Students export.
2. Internships export.
3. International Opportunities export.

For every export:
- Fix the frontend button and API request.
- Ensure the backend generates a valid downloadable CSV.
- Verify the filename, extension, response headers, encoding, CSV escaping, and data values.
- Handle empty datasets and errors correctly.
- Enforce the existing role-based authorization policy.
- Prevent unnecessary exposure of confidential information.
- Mitigate CSV formula injection where applicable.
- Create audit records for successful exports according to the intended application behavior.

Use automated HTTP tests to verify actual responses and downloaded CSV content. Do not count a visible button as a successful export.

### STEP 5 — FIX EXPORT AUDIT HISTORY

Repair `/api/analytics/export-audit/` and the corresponding frontend page.

- Fix authorization and response structure.
- Fix export-type filtering.
- Fix newest-first ordering.
- Fix pagination metadata and Previous/Next controls.
- Fix loading, empty, and error states.
- Verify that successful exports produce accurate audit records.
- Ensure failed exports are not falsely marked as successful.
- Ensure audit records do not unnecessarily contain tokens, credentials, or exported personal data.

Add and execute automated tests for these behaviors.

### STEP 6 — AUTOMATICALLY FIX FAILING TESTS

Run the existing tests first.

Then:
1. Capture the actual failures.
2. Inspect the relevant code and error messages.
3. Fix the root cause of each project-related failure.
4. Rerun the failing tests.
5. Rerun the complete relevant test suite.
6. Check that no unrelated Phase 5 functionality has regressed.

Do not suppress errors, skip required tests without justification, or weaken security assertions.

### STEP 7 — RUN THE REQUIRED CHECKS

Frontend:
- `npm run build`
- `npm run lint`
- Existing frontend tests, if available.

Backend:
- `python manage.py check`
- Relevant Django tests.
- `python manage.py showmigrations`
- Actual database connection verification.
- Analytics, export, audit, and permission tests.

Use the project's actual interpreter and working directory. Record real command exit codes.

### STEP 8 — HANDLE UNAVAILABLE DEPENDENCIES PROPERLY

If a dependency is genuinely unavailable:

1. Diagnose the exact cause.
2. Fix it if possible using the existing environment and available permissions.
3. If elevated permissions, installation, credentials, or external access are required, identify the precise action needed.
4. Continue implementing and testing everything that does not depend on that blocker.
5. Use isolated automated tests where feasible.
6. Clearly separate verified results from remaining manual checks.

Do not report `BLOCKED` as a substitute for attempting a reasonable fix. Do not claim a fix succeeded when the environment does not permit it.

### STEP 9 — STRICT COMPLETION RULE

Phase 6 is complete only when the required functionality and security checks have actual passing evidence:

- [ ] Staff Overview displays real API data.
- [ ] All three CSV exports work.
- [ ] Export filenames, headers, and contents are verified.
- [ ] Audit creation, filtering, and pagination work.
