# Phase 5: Documents + Profile + Resume

Phase 4 ची तपासणी पूर्ण झाल्यावरच हा Phase द्या. यामुळे प्रत्येक विद्यार्थ्याचा पूर्ण profile तयार होतो, Offer Letter आणि Certificate जमा होतात आणि Resume आपोआप बनतो.

## या Phase मध्ये काय बनतं

| भाग                  | कोण वापरतो        | काम                                                             |
| -------------------- | ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| My Profile           | Student           | Basic Details, Education, Skills, Projects, Certifications भरणे |
| Documents Upload     | Student           | Offer Letter, LOR, Certificate, Other upload करणे               |
| My Internship page   | Student           | निवडलेल्या internship ची details आणि त्याचे documents           |
| Documents View       | Coordinator/Admin | Student detail page वर सर्व documents बघणे आणि download करणे    |
| Resume Generate      | Student           | Profile वरून आपोआप PDF Resume                                   |
| Profile Completeness | Student           | "Profile 70% पूर्ण" असा progress                                |

## Profile चे Sections

| Section        | Fields                                                                  |
| -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Basic Details  | Full name, PRN, branch, year, phone, bio (200 अक्षरं), LinkedIn, GitHub |
| Education      | Degree, College, Year, CGPA (अनेक entries)                              |
| Skills         | Tags (उदा. Python, React)                                               |
| Projects       | Title, Description, Tech used, Link (अनेक entries)                      |
| Certifications | Name, Issuer, Date, Link (अनेक entries)                                 |

## Documents चे नियम

| नियम       | तपशील                                   |
| ---------- | --------------------------------------- |
| File types | PDF, JPG, PNG                           |
| कमाल size  | 5 MB प्रत्येकी                          |
| Types      | OfferLetter, LOR, Certificate, Other    |
| Student    | फक्त स्वतःचे documents बघतो/delete करतो |
| Staff      | सर्व बघू/download करू शकतो, delete नाही |
| Storage    | Private bucket, signed URL ने उघडतात    |

## Phase 5 Prompt (Copy-Paste)
```
PHASE 5 — DOCUMENTS, PROFILE, RESUME

Build on top of Phases 0 to 4. Do NOT modify or break any existing feature. Only add the following and fill the existing "My Profile", "My Internship", and "Resume" student pages, and extend the staff student detail page.

A) DATABASE ADDITIONS (SQL migration, additive only)
- Create table student_profile_details if it does not exist: student_id (pk, references profiles.id), bio, linkedin_url, github_url, education (jsonb array), skills (text[]), projects (jsonb array), certifications (jsonb array), updated_at.
- Extend documents table with: student_internship_id (nullable), file_name, file_size, and keep type (OfferLetter|LOR|Certificate|Other).
- Use the private Storage bucket "documents". File path format: <student_id>/<uuid>-<file_name>.

B) STUDENT — "My Profile" page
1. Sections: Basic Details (full name, PRN, branch, year, phone, bio max 200 chars, LinkedIn URL, GitHub URL), Education (add/edit/remove entries: degree, college, year, CGPA), Skills (tag input, max 30), Projects (add/edit/remove: title, description, tech used, link), Certifications (add/edit/remove: name, issuer, date, link).
2. Each section has its own Save button with a toast; validate URLs and required fields.
3. Profile completeness bar (Basic 20%, Education 20%, Skills 20%, Projects 20%, Certifications 20%). Show it on My Profile and Student Home with a hint on what is missing.

C) STUDENT — "My Internship" page
1. Show the student's internships with status Selected, Ongoing, or Completed as cards/tabs. Each shows details, start/end dates, status, and report count.
2. Documents area per internship: upload button with a type selector (OfferLetter | LOR | Certificate | Other). Accept only PDF, JPG, PNG up to 5 MB, validate on both client and server. Show upload progress.
3. List uploaded documents with name, type, size, date, a View/Download button (signed URL, expires in 60 seconds), and Delete (own documents only, with confirmation).
4. If no internship qualifies, show a friendly message linking to the Internships tab.

D) STAFF — extend the student detail page (/staff/students/:id)
1. Add a "Documents" section listing all of that student's documents with View/Download (signed URL). Staff cannot delete.
2. Add a "Profile" section showing the student's bio, education, skills, projects, certifications, and links (read-only).
3. Add a "Download Resume" button that generates the same PDF as the student's Resume page.

E) STUDENT — "Resume" page
1. "Generate Resume" button builds a clean, single-page, ATS-friendly PDF in the browser from: name, contact (email, phone, LinkedIn, GitHub), bio, education, skills, projects, internships (Ongoing/Completed with company, role/title, duration), and certifications.
2. Show a live preview on the page before download. Sections with no data are skipped; if the profile is under 40% complete, show a warning with a link to My Profile.
3. Provide one simple template (clean, black text, indigo section headings). Download file name: <Full_Name>_Resume.pdf.

F) NOTIFICATIONS
- When a student uploads a Certificate or Offer Letter, notify all staff ("<name> uploaded <type>") linking to that student's detail page.

G) SECURITY (RLS and Storage policies)
- student_profile_details: a student can read/insert/update only their own row; staff can read all.
- documents table and Storage bucket: a student can insert, read, and delete only their own files (folder = their user id); staff can read all but cannot delete or modify.
- Enforce the 5 MB and file-type limits at the storage/policy level too, not only in the UI.
- Signed URLs only; never make the bucket public.

ACCEPTANCE CHECKLIST — report each item as PASS or FAIL and fix any FAIL
[ ] Student can fill and save all 5 profile sections; data persists after refresh
[ ] Invalid URLs and missing required fields are rejected
[ ] Profile completeness % updates correctly
[ ] Student can upload PDF/JPG/PNG up to 5 MB; other types and larger files are rejected
[ ] Uploaded documents open via a signed URL that expires; direct public URL does not work
[ ] Student can delete only their own documents; cannot see another student's (verify RLS)
[ ] Staff can view and download every student's documents but cannot delete them
[ ] Staff gets a notification when a student uploads a Certificate or Offer Letter
[ ] Resume preview shows correct data; the PDF downloads with the right file name
[ ] Empty sections are skipped in the Resume; low-completeness warning appears
[ ] Staff can view a student's profile and download that student's Resume
[ ] Everything works properly on a mobile screen

```

## Phase 3 — Updated Final Prompt

:::writing{variant="document" id="58392"}
# PHASE 3 — WEEKLY PROGRESS REPORTS, STAFF REVIEW, AND REAL-DATA INTEGRATION

## Project
Internship Performance Tracking System (IPTS) / Career Growth Hub

Act as a senior full-stack engineer. Work directly in my existing project workspace.

Implement and complete Phase 3 using the existing Weekly Progress Reports form, report list, API endpoints, review workflow, database models, and dashboard components.

**Do not create a new report system from scratch. Inspect the existing implementation first, fix its problems, and preserve all working functionality.**

## 1. MANDATORY PROJECT INSPECTION

Before modifying code:

1. Inspect the existing React + TypeScript frontend and the actual backend architecture.
2. Inspect the existing Weekly Progress Reports form and the code for:
   - `handleSubmitReport`
   - `handleResubmit`
   - `handleDeleteReport`
   - `openReviewModal`
   - `handleFeedbackSubmit`
   - `getStatusBadge`
   - `fetchReports`
   - `validateRequired`
3. Inspect the existing `api` client and confirm how authentication, errors, requests, and responses are handled.
4. Inspect the backend report model, serializers, views/viewsets, URLs, permissions, and database migrations.
5. Verify the actual behavior of:
   - `POST /reports/`
   - `PATCH /reports/:id/`
   - `DELETE /reports/:id/`
   - `POST /reports/:id/feedback/`
6. Confirm the actual database relationships between students, internships, student-internship records, and weekly reports.
7. Inspect the existing Student Home, Staff Overview, Report Reviews, Students, and Notifications pages.
8. Reuse the current API, database, components, and design system.
9. Do not assume that the project uses Supabase. Preserve the backend that actually exists.
10. If Phases 0, 1, or 2 are incomplete, document the blocker and do not make unrelated architectural changes.

Do not begin Phase 4.

## 2. PRESERVE THE EXISTING REPORT MODEL AND STATUS WORKFLOW

The current frontend uses these status values:

- `DRAFT`
- `SUBMITTED`
- `UNDER_REVIEW`
- `APPROVED`
- `NEEDS_IMPROVEMENT`

Inspect the backend to confirm which statuses it supports.

Use the existing status values and database representation consistently. Do not introduce duplicate or conflicting status names such as `PENDING` unless a deliberate, backward-compatible migration is necessary.

Expected workflow:

1. Student creates a draft or submits a report.
2. Submitted reports become available to authorized staff for review.
3. Staff reviews the report and approves it or marks it as needing improvement.
4. A report needing improvement can be edited and resubmitted.
5. An approved report is read-only to the student.
6. Report status, review comments, timestamps, and progress remain consistent after refreshing or logging in again.

Use backend-enforced permissions for all status transitions.

If the existing implementation has a legitimate additional status, preserve it and document its purpose.

### Progress Calculation

Use:

`Progress % = min(100, approved reports / expected reports × 100)`

Expected reports are based on the number of expected reporting weeks between the internship start date and the current date, with a minimum of one expected report.

Requirements:

- Use the actual internship start date.
- Do not invent missing dates.
- Avoid division by zero.
- Count only approved reports in the progress numerator.
- Do not count draft or needs-improvement reports as approved.
- Define how an approved report contributes to a reporting week.
- Calculate consistently using the project's date and timezone conventions.
- Avoid counting duplicate reports more than once.

### Reporting Streak

Calculate consecutive reporting weeks from actual reports.

- Do not count multiple reports from the same week more than once.
- Do not count future weeks.
- Use the actual submission timestamp and week number according to a documented convention.
- Handle missed weeks and empty histories correctly.

Do not use hardcoded percentages or sample progress figures.

## मी कोणत्या महत्त्वाच्या सुधारणा समाविष्ट केल्या?

- **Draft आणि Submit\:** दोन्ही वेळा चुकीने नवीन report तयार होणार नाही, यासाठी backend API चा व्यवहार तपासण्याची अट.
- **Resubmit\:** `NEEDS_IMPROVEMENT` report योग्यरीत्या पुन्हा submit होईल.
- **Duplicate Week\:** एकाच internship साठी एकाच week चा दुसरा report तयार होणार नाही.
- **Staff Review\:** feedback, decision आणि status हे backend सोबत सुसंगत राहतील.
- **Approved Reports\:** विद्यार्थ्यांना मंजूर report बदलता येणार नाही.
- **Real Data\:** बनावट reports, counts किंवा progress टाळले जातील.
- **Existing Architecture\:** Django/backend API आणि सध्याचे React components वापरले जातील; duplicate system तयार होणार नाही.

आता हा prompt Antigravity मध्ये दे. त्याला **आधी code आणि backend तपासून मगच बदल करायला** सांगितले आहे, त्यामुळे तुझ्या सध्याच्या form मधील उपयुक्त fields अनावश्यकपणे काढून टाकले जाणार नाहीत.

### Progress Calculation

Use:

`Progress % = min(100, approved reports / expected reports × 100)`

Expected reports are based on the number of expected reporting weeks between the internship start date and the current date, with a minimum of one expected report.

Requirements:

- Use the actual internship start date.
- Do not invent missing dates.
- Avoid division by zero.
- Count only approved reports in the progress numerator.
- Do not count draft or needs-improvement reports as approved.
- Define how an approved report contributes to a reporting week.
- Calculate consistently using the project's date and timezone conventions.
- Avoid counting duplicate reports more than once.

### Reporting Streak

Calculate consecutive reporting weeks from actual reports.

- Do not count multiple reports from the same week more than once.
- Do not count future weeks.
- Use the actual submission timestamp and week number according to a documented convention.
- Handle missed weeks and empty histories correctly.

Do not use hardcoded percentages or sample progress figures.

## मी कोणत्या महत्त्वाच्या सुधारणा समाविष्ट केल्या?

- **Draft आणि Submit:** दोन्ही वेळा चुकीने नवीन report तयार होणार नाही, यासाठी backend API चा व्यवहार तपासण्याची अट.
- **Resubmit:** `NEEDS_IMPROVEMENT` report योग्यरीत्या पुन्हा submit होईल.
- **Duplicate Week:** एकाच internship साठी एकाच week चा दुसरा report तयार होणार नाही.
- **Staff Review:** feedback, decision आणि status हे backend सोबत सुसंगत राहतील.
- **Approved Reports:** विद्यार्थ्यांना मंजूर report बदलता येणार नाही.
- **Real Data:** बनावट reports, counts किंवा progress टाळले जातील.
- **Existing Architecture:** Django/backend API आणि सध्याचे React components वापरले जातील; duplicate system तयार होणार नाही.

आता हा prompt Antigravity मध्ये दे. त्याला **आधी code आणि backend तपासून मगच बदल करायला** सांगितले आहे, त्यामुळे तुझ्या सध्याच्या form मधील उपयुक्त fields अनावश्यकपणे काढून टाकले जाणार नाहीत.

  const handleSubmitReport = async (status: 'DRAFT' | 'SUBMITTED') => {
    if (!validateRequired()) return;
    setSaving(true);
    setMessage(null);

    try {
      const payload = {
        internship: selectedInternshipId!,
        week_number: formData.week_number,
        tasks_completed: formData.tasks_completed,
        technical_skills: formData.technical_skills,
        learning_outcomes: formData.learning_outcomes,
        challenges_faced: formData.challenges_faced,
        solutions_implemented: formData.solutions_implemented,
        project_progress: formData.project_progress,
        github_link: formData.github_link,
        demo_link: formData.demo_link,
        next_week_plan: formData.next_week_plan,
        student_reflection: formData.student_reflection,
        hours_worked: parseInt(formData.hours_worked),
        proof_links: formData.proof_links.filter(l => l.trim()),
        status,
      };

      if (status === 'SUBMITTED') {
        await api.post('/reports/', payload);
        setMessage({ type: 'success', text: 'Week ' + formData.week_number + ' report submitted successfully!' });
      } else {
        await api.post('/reports/', payload);
        setMessage({ type: 'success', text: 'Week ' + formData.week_number + ' draft saved.' });
      }

      setFormData(prev => ({
        ...prev,
        week_number: prev.week_number + 1,
        tasks_completed: '',
        technical_skills: '',
        learning_outcomes: '',
        challenges_faced: '',
        solutions_implemented: '',
        project_progress: '',
        github_link: '',
        demo_link: '',
        next_week_plan: '',
        student_reflection: '',
      }));
      fetchReports();
    } catch (err: any) {
      setMessage({ type: 'error', text: err.message || 'Failed to save report' });
    } finally {
      setSaving(false);
    }
  };

  const handleResubmit = async () => {
    if (!activeReport) return;
    if (activeReport.status === 'SUBMITTED') {
      setMessage({ type: 'error', text: 'This report is already submitted.' });
      return;
    }
    if (!formData.tasks_completed.trim() || !formData.technical_skills.trim() || !formData.learning_outcomes.trim()) {
      setMessage({ type: 'error', text: 'Please fill in Tasks Completed, Technical Skills, and Learning Outcomes.' });
      return;
    }

    try {
      await api.patch('/reports/' + activeReport.id + '/', {
        tasks_completed: formData.tasks_completed,
        technical_skills: formData.technical_skills,
        learning_outcomes: formData.learning_outcomes,
        challenges_faced: formData.challenges_faced,
        solutions_implemented: formData.solutions_implemented,
        project_progress: formData.project_progress,
        github_link: formData.github_link,
        demo_link: formData.demo_link,
        next_week_plan: formData.next_week_plan,
        student_reflection: formData.student_reflection,
        hours_worked: parseInt(formData.hours_worked),
        proof_links: formData.proof_links.filter(l => l.trim()),
        status: 'SUBMITTED',
      });
      setMessage({ type: 'success', text: 'Report resubmitted successfully!' });
      fetchReports();
    } catch (err: any) {
      setMessage({ type: 'error', text: err.message || 'Failed to resubmit report' });
    }
  };

  const handleDeleteReport = async (id: number) => {
    if (!window.confirm('Delete this draft report?')) return;
    try {
      await api.delete('/reports/' + id + '/');
      setMessage({ type: 'success', text: 'Report deleted.' });
      fetchReports();
    } catch (err: any) {
      setMessage({ type: 'error', text: err.message || 'Failed to delete report' });
    }
  };

  const openReviewModal = (report: ProgressReport) => {
    setActiveReport(report);
    setFeedbackForm({ score: 8, comments: '', decision: 'APPROVED', improvement_task: '' });
  };

  const handleFeedbackSubmit = async (decision: 'APPROVED' | 'NEEDS_IMPROVEMENT') => {
    if (!activeReport) return;
    setSaving(true);
    try {
      await api.post('/reports/' + activeReport.id + '/feedback/', {
        score: feedbackForm.score,
        comments: feedbackForm.comments,
        decision,
        task_title: feedbackForm.improvement_task,
      });
      setMessage({ type: 'success', text: 'Report ' + (decision === 'APPROVED' ? 'approved' : 'marked for improvement') + '.' });
      setActiveReport(null);
      fetchReports();
    } catch (err: any) {
      setMessage({ type: 'error', text: err.message || 'Failed to submit feedback' });
    } finally { setSaving(false); }
  };

  const getStatusBadge = (status: string) => {
    switch (status) {
      case 'APPROVED': return <span className="badge badge-success">Approved</span>;
      case 'NEEDS_IMPROVEMENT': return <span className="badge badge-warning">Needs Improvement</span>;
      case 'SUBMITTED': return <span className="badge badge-published">Submitted</span>;
      case 'DRAFT': return <span className="badge badge-secondary">Draft</span>;
      case 'UNDER_REVIEW': return <span className="badge badge-info">Under Review</span>;
      default: return <span className="badge badge-secondary">{status}</span>;
    }
  };

  const formatDate = (dateStr: string | null) => {
    if (!dateStr) return '-';
    try { return new Date(dateStr).toLocaleDateString('en-US', { year: 'numeric', month: 'short', day: 'numeric' }); }

# PHASE 4 — COMMUNITY CHAT, ANNOUNCEMENTS, AND REAL-DATA-ONLY INTEGRATION

## Project
Internship Performance Tracking System (IPTS) / Career Growth Hub

Act as a senior full-stack engineer working directly in my existing project workspace.

Implement Phase 4 only: Community Chat, Announcements, Moderation, Announcement Notifications, and the Student Home Announcements Widget.

**The entire existing website must continue working with real database data. Do not introduce dummy data, mock records, hardcoded statistics, fake notifications, or sample content.**

## 1. MANDATORY EXISTING PROJECT INSPECTION

Before making any changes:

1. Inspect the entire existing project structure, frontend, backend, routes, components, layouts, database schema, migrations, authentication, permissions, and API services.
2. Inspect the actual technology stack. Preserve the existing backend and database architecture. Do not assume Supabase if the project uses Django or another backend.
3. Verify Phases 0, 1, 2, and 3, including authentication, roles, internship management, weekly reports, reviews, and notifications.
4. Identify all existing database tables and relationships.
5. Inspect existing Student, Coordinator, and Admin dashboards and navigation.
6. Identify all existing demo, seed, mock, test, and hardcoded data sources.
7. Identify which records are genuine user/application data and which records are explicitly designated demo/test data.
8. Reuse existing working components, APIs, tables, authentication, notification infrastructure, and styling wherever possible.
9. Do not recreate existing features or introduce a second authentication, database, or notification system.
10. If an earlier phase is broken, report the blocker and avoid unrelated rewrites.

Do not start Phase 5.

## 2. STRICT REAL-DATA-ONLY REQUIREMENT

The website must use actual records returned by the configured backend and database.

### Remove Dummy Data From the Application

Inspect all existing pages and remove demo/mock data usage from runtime application screens, including:

- Hardcoded student lists
- Fake internship records
- Sample weekly reports
- Mock chat messages
- Fake announcements
- Hardcoded dashboard statistics
- Fake notification records
- Placeholder analytics presented as real results
- Fallback arrays that silently display fabricated records when an API request fails

Replace these sources with real backend API/database queries wherever the corresponding feature exists.

### Database Data Cleanup Rules

Before deleting any existing records:

1. Identify the exact records that are explicitly demo, mock, test, or seed data.
2. Explain which tables contain those records and what relationships depend on them.
3. Create an appropriate backup or export before any approved destructive cleanup.
4. Delete only records that can be reliably identified as demo/test data and are authorized for deletion.
5. Preserve genuine student accounts, staff accounts, profiles, internships, applications, reports, review history, documents, and notifications.
6. Do not truncate tables, reset the database, drop tables, or delete all users to achieve a clean interface.
7. Do not assume that an old record is dummy data merely because it is old.
8. Do not remove production data simply because it is not currently displayed.
9. If a record's classification is uncertain, preserve it and report it for manual review.
10. Never silently delete or overwrite existing data.

**Important:** Do not create new dummy data to replace deleted records. New records must be created only through the actual application's authorized user workflows.

If test records need to be created for verification, use a separate test environment or explicitly designated test accounts, not production student records.

## 3. NO FAKE DATA OR SILENT FALLBACKS

Every page must follow these rules:

- Fetch real data from the configured backend.
- Show a genuine empty state when no records exist.
- Show an appropriate loading state while fetching data.
- Show a clear error when a database/API request fails.
- Never replace an API error with fabricated sample data.
- Never report fake success when a database operation fails.
- Never display invented student counts, report counts, unread counts, or message counts.
- Do not insert example announcements, sample messages, or fake notifications during application startup.
- Do not add automatic seed scripts that populate the live database.
- Do not silently fall back to browser local storage as the source of truth for persistent shared data.
- Do not treat cached data as authoritative when the server reports an error.

All shared application data must be persisted and retrieved through the existing authorized backend.

## 4. PHASE 4 — COMMUNITY PAGE

Complete the existing Community pages for Student, Coordinator, and Admin.

Reuse the existing sidebar navigation and page layout.

Provide two channels:

- `#announcements`
- `#community`

Both channels must use real database records.

### A. Community Chat

Implement the following:

1. Display the latest 50 real messages.
2. Add a `Load older messages` button with correct pagination.
3. Display sender name, role badge, timestamp, and message content.
4. Support real-time delivery using the existing backend's supported real-time mechanism.
5. If the existing architecture does not support real-time events, implement a suitable server-backed alternative without introducing a duplicate backend.
6. Show new messages without requiring a full page refresh.
7. Auto-scroll to the newest message only when the user is already near the bottom.
8. Preserve the user's scroll position when loading older messages.
9. Allow text and legitimate URLs.
10. Automatically link URLs safely, opening them in a new tab with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.
11. Render messages as plain text. Never execute message HTML.
12. Support Enter to send and Shift+Enter for a newline.
13. Limit messages to 1,000 characters.
14. Reject empty messages.
15. Enforce one message per user per five-second interval on the server.
16. Show a friendly rate-limit message when a user sends too quickly.
17. Disable the send control while a request is in progress.
18. Display real loading, empty, and error states.

### Message Deletion

- Students can soft-delete their own messages.
- Staff can soft-delete any community message.
- Deleted messages display `This message was deleted`.
- Deleted content must not remain readable through unauthorized direct API/database requests.
- Preserve audit information where appropriate.
- Do not permanently delete unrelated user or application records.

### Muted Students

When a student is muted:

- The student can still read the community channel.
- The student cannot send new messages.
- The input is replaced with `You are muted by a coordinator`.
- The server/database must reject unauthorized message submissions even if the user bypasses the frontend.

## 5. ANNOUNCEMENTS CHANNEL

Display actual announcements, ordered with pinned announcements first and then by newest creation date.

### Student Permissions

Students can:

- Read announcements.
- Open announcement details.
- Navigate to the announcement from notifications.
- See pinned announcements and recent announcements on Student Home.

Students cannot create, edit, delete, or pin announcements.

### Staff Permissions

Coordinator and Admin can:

- Create announcements.
- Edit announcements.
- Delete announcements.
- Pin and unpin announcements.

The creation form must contain:

- Title — required
- Body — required
- Pin this announcement — checkbox

Validate all required fields and display clear errors.

Limit the number of pinned announcements to three.

Enforce the three-pinned-announcements limit on the server/database, including concurrent requests. Do not rely only on the frontend.

If the limit is reached, display a clear message explaining that another announcement must be unpinned first.

Use actual database records for all operations.

## 6. STAFF MODERATION

### Mute / Unmute

Coordinator and Admin can mute or unmute students.

Requirements:

- Add a Mute/Unmute action to the relevant student message menu.
- Add a `Muted` badge and Mute/Unmute action to the existing Staff → Students detail page.
- Update the existing profile record or equivalent user moderation record.
- Prevent staff from muting other staff members.
- Prevent students from changing their own mute status.
- Enforce permissions through the backend/database.
- Record the acting staff user and timestamp if the existing audit architecture supports it.
- Display clear success and error messages.

Do not change unrelated student profile information.

## 7. REAL-TIME ANNOUNCEMENT NOTIFICATIONS

When staff creates a new announcement:

1. Save the announcement successfully.
2. Generate notifications for eligible, approved students using the trusted backend.
3. Use the message format:

   `New announcement: <title>`

4. Link each notification to the Community page's announcements channel.
5. Update the existing notification bell and unread count.
6. Prevent duplicate notifications caused by retries or repeated requests.
7. Do not create notifications for unapproved accounts unless explicitly required by the existing authorization model.
8. Do not fabricate notifications or show success when notification creation fails.

Use the existing notification table and infrastructure.

Do not notify users before the announcement has been successfully saved.

## 8. STUDENT HOME — ANNOUNCEMENTS WIDGET

Add an `Announcements` section to the existing Student Home page.

Display a maximum of three announcements:

1. Pinned announcements first.
2. Remaining slots filled by the newest announcements.
3. Each item shows its title and publication date.
4. Each item links to the corresponding announcement in the Community page.
5. Fetch all content from the real backend.
6. Show a useful empty state if no announcements exist.

Do not create a duplicate Student Home page.

Preserve existing dashboard cards, internship progress, and report information.

## 9. UNREAD COMMUNITY INDICATOR

Add an unread dot to the existing Community sidebar item when there is new activity since the user last viewed the relevant channel.

Use the existing architecture or create a minimal `channel_reads` table if required.

Logical fields:

- `user_id`
- `channel`
- `last_seen_at`

Requirements:

- Store last-seen state per authenticated user and channel.
- Support `community` and `announcements`.
- Update last-seen state when the user opens the relevant channel.
- Clear the relevant unread indicator only after the appropriate channel has been opened and its latest content has been loaded successfully.
- Do not mark content as seen for other users.
- Use actual timestamps and database records.
- Prevent unauthorized users from reading or updating another user's channel-read state.
- Do not rely only on local storage for cross-device unread state.

If the current architecture has a suitable existing read-tracking mechanism, reuse it instead of creating duplicate tables.

## 10. DATABASE MIGRATIONS

Inspect the existing database before creating migrations.

Reuse existing tables wherever possible.

Ensure the data model supports the equivalent of:

### Messages

- `id`
- `sender_id`
- `channel`
- `content`
- `deleted`
- `deleted_by`
- `created_at`
- `updated_at`

### Announcements

- `id`
- `title`
- `body`
- `pinned`
- `created_by`
- `created_at`
- `updated_at`

### Profile Moderation

- Existing user/profile relationship
- `muted`, default false, if not already available

### Channel Reads

- `user_id`
- `channel`
- `last_seen_at`

Adapt names and relationships to the existing schema.

Use safe, additive, version-controlled migrations.

Do not recreate existing tables, erase existing data, or introduce duplicate fields.

Ensure the schema supports:

- Valid sender relationships
- Valid channel names
- Message length constraints
- Safe soft deletion
- Rate limiting
- Pinned announcement limits
- Appropriate foreign keys and indexes
- Authorized per-user read tracking

Enable real-time subscriptions only if supported by the actual backend and current configuration.

If using Django, use its existing migrations and backend conventions. If using Supabase, use its existing PostgreSQL migrations and security model. Do not mix architectures unnecessarily.

## 11. SECURITY AND AUTHORIZATION

Enforce security on the server/database. Frontend controls alone are insufficient.

### Read Permissions

- Approved users can read authorized, non-deleted community messages.
- Approved students and staff can read announcements according to the existing access rules.
- Users cannot access private data outside their authorization scope.

### Message Insert Permissions

- Approved, non-muted students can post in `community`.
- Authorized staff can post in `community`.
- Only authorized staff can create announcements.
- The sender identity must come from the authenticated server-side identity.
- Students cannot impersonate another sender.
- Students cannot send messages while muted.

### Message Update Permissions

- Users can soft-delete only their own messages.
- Authorized staff can soft-delete community messages.
- Users cannot edit existing message content through update requests.
- Users cannot change another user's message, sender ID, role, or moderation fields.

### Announcement Permissions

- Only authorized Coordinator/Admin users can create, edit, delete, pin, or unpin announcements.
- Students cannot bypass read-only permissions using direct API/database requests.
- The three-pinned-announcements limit must be enforced server-side.

### Mute Permissions

- Only authorized staff can mute/unmute students.
- Staff cannot mute other staff.
- Students cannot mute/unmute themselves.
- The backend must reject unauthorized attempts.

### Rate Limiting

- Enforce one message per five-second interval per authenticated user on the server.
- Handle concurrent requests safely.
- Do not rely solely on JavaScript timers.

### General Security

- Never expose service-role keys or other backend secrets in frontend code.
- Validate all incoming data on the server.
- Prevent XSS and open redirects.
- Protect existing Phase 1 role permissions.
- Preserve Phase 2 internship security and Phase 3 report security.
- Do not weaken existing authorization policies.

## 12. PRESERVE EXISTING WEBSITE DESIGN AND FUNCTIONALITY

This is an incremental feature implementation.

Do not:

- Rebuild the website.
- Replace the existing frontend framework or backend.
- Change authentication or registration flows.
- Delete genuine student or staff accounts.
- Remove existing internships, reports, review history, or legitimate notifications.
- Change unrelated database schemas.
- Remove existing dashboard cards or sidebar entries.
- Redesign existing pages unnecessarily.
- Replace real database queries with sample data.
- Introduce unrelated features.
- Start Phase 5.

Keep the existing logo, visual identity, layouts, and navigation.

Only make the changes needed for Phase 4.

## 13. ACCEPTANCE TESTS

Run the actual tests available and report every item as PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED.

Fix all resolvable failures.

1. Two authorized accounts in separate browsers see new community messages in real time.
2. Messages display the correct sender, role, time, and content.

15. Enforce one message per user per five-second interval on the server.
16. Show a friendly rate-limit message when a user sends too quickly.
17. Disable the send control while a request is in progress.
18. Display real loading, empty, and error states.

### Message Deletion

- Students can soft-delete their own messages.
- Staff can soft-delete any community message.
- Deleted messages display `This message was deleted`.
- Deleted content must not remain readable through unauthorized direct API/database requests.
- Preserve audit information where appropriate.
- Do not permanently delete unrelated user or application records.

### Muted Students

When a student is muted:

- The student can still read the community channel.
- The student cannot send new messages.
- The input is replaced with `You are muted by a coordinator`.
- The server/database must reject unauthorized message submissions even if the user bypasses the frontend.

Use actual database records for all operations.

Before making any changes:

1. Inspect the entire existing project structure, frontend, backend, routes, components, layouts, database schema, migrations, authentication, permissions, and API services.
2. Inspect the actual technology stack. Preserve the existing backend and database architecture. Do not assume Supabase if the project uses Django or another backend.
3. Verify Phases 0, 1, 2, and 3, including authentication, roles, internship management, weekly reports, reviews, and notifications.
4. Identify all existing database tables and relationships.
5. Inspect existing Student, Coordinator, and Admin dashboards and navigation.
6. Identify all existing demo, seed, mock, test, and hardcoded data sources.
7. Identify which records are genuine user/application data and which records are explicitly designated demo/test data.
8. Reuse existing working components, APIs, tables, authentication, notification infrastructure, and styling wherever possible.
9. Do not recreate existing features or introduce a second authentication, database, or notification system.
10. If an earlier phase is broken, report the blocker and avoid unrelated rewrites.

Do not start Phase 5.

## 2. STRICT REAL-DATA-ONLY REQUIREMENT

The website must use actual records returned by the configured backend and database.

### Remove Dummy Data From the Application

Inspect all existing pages and remove demo/mock data usage from runtime application screens, including:

- Hardcoded student lists
- Fake internship records
- Sample weekly reports
- Mock chat messages
- Fake announcements
- Hardcoded dashboard statistics
- Fake notification records
- Placeholder analytics presented as real results
- Fallback arrays that silently display fabricated records when an API request fails

Replace these sources with real backend API/database queries wherever the corresponding feature exists.

### Database Data Cleanup Rules

Before deleting any existing records:

1. Identify the exact records that are explicitly demo, mock, test, or seed data.
2. Explain which tables contain those records and what relationships depend on them.
3. Create an appropriate backup or export before any approved destructive cleanup.
4. Delete only records that can be reliably identified as demo/test data and are authorized for deletion.
5. Preserve genuine student accounts, staff accounts, profiles, internships, applications, reports, review history, documents, and notifications.
6. Do not truncate tables, reset the database, drop tables, or delete all users to achieve a clean interface.
7. Do not assume that an old record is dummy data merely because it is old.
8. Do not remove production data simply because it is not currently displayed.
9. If a record's classification is uncertain, preserve it and report it for manual review.
10. Never silently delete or overwrite existing data.

**Important:** Do not create new dummy data to replace deleted records. New records must be created only through the actual application's authorized user workflows.

If test records need to be created for verification, use a separate test environment or explicitly designated test accounts, not production student records.

## 3. NO FAKE DATA OR SILENT FALLBACKS

Every page must follow these rules:

- Fetch real data from the configured backend.
- Show a genuine empty state when no records exist.
- Show an appropriate loading state while fetching data.
- Show a clear error when a database/API request fails.
- Never replace an API error with fabricated sample data.
- Never report fake success when a database operation fails.
- Never display invented student counts, report counts, unread counts, or message counts.
- Do not insert example announcements, sample messages, or fake notifications during application startup.
- Do not add automatic seed scripts that populate the live database.
- Do not silently fall back to browser local storage as the source of truth for persistent shared data.
- Do not treat cached data as authoritative when the server reports an error.

All shared application data must be persisted and retrieved through the existing authorized backend.

## 4. PHASE 4 — COMMUNITY PAGE

Complete the existing Community pages for Student, Coordinator, and Admin.

Reuse the existing sidebar navigation and page layout.

Provide two channels:

- `#announcements`
- `#community`

Both channels must use real database records.

### A. Community Chat

Implement the following:

1. Display the latest 50 real messages.
2. Add a `Load older messages` button with correct pagination.
3. Display sender name, role badge, timestamp, and message content.
4. Support real-time delivery using the existing backend's supported real-time mechanism.
5. If the existing architecture does not support real-time events, implement a suitable server-backed alternative without introducing a duplicate backend.
6. Show new messages without requiring a full page refresh.
7. Auto-scroll to the newest message only when the user is already near the bottom.
8. Preserve the user's scroll position when loading older messages.
9. Allow text and legitimate URLs.
10. Automatically link URLs safely, opening them in a new tab with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.
11. Render messages as plain text. Never execute message HTML.
12. Support Enter to send and Shift+Enter for a newline.
13. Limit messages to 1,000 characters.
14. Reject empty messages.
15. Enforce one message per user per five-second interval on the server.
16. Show a friendly rate-limit message when a user sends too quickly.
17. Disable the send control while a request is in progress.
18. Display real loading, empty, and error states.

### Message Deletion

- Students can soft-delete their own messages.
- Staff can soft-delete any community message.
- Deleted messages display `This message was deleted`.
- Deleted content must not remain readable through unauthorized direct API/database requests.
- Preserve audit information where appropriate.
- Do not permanently delete unrelated user or application records.

### Muted Students

When a student is muted:

- The student can still read the community channel.
- The student cannot send new messages.
- The input is replaced with `You are muted by a coordinator`.
- The server/database must reject unauthorized message submissions even if the user bypasses the frontend.

## 5. ANNOUNCEMENTS CHANNEL

Display actual announcements, ordered with pinned announcements first and then by newest creation date.

### Student Permissions

Students can:

- Read announcements.
- Open announcement details.
- Navigate to the announcement from notifications.
- See pinned announcements and recent announcements on Student Home.

Students cannot create, edit, delete, or pin announcements.

### Staff Permissions

Coordinator and Admin can:

- Create announcements.
- Edit announcements.
- Delete announcements.
- Pin and unpin announcements.

The creation form must contain:

- Title — required
- Body — required
- Pin this announcement — checkbox

Validate all required fields and display clear errors.

Limit the number of pinned announcements to three.

Enforce the three-pinned-announcements limit on the server/database, including concurrent requests. Do not rely only on the frontend.

If the limit is reached, display a clear message explaining that another announcement must be unpinned first.

Use actual database records for all operations.

## 6. STAFF MODERATION

### Mute / Unmute

Coordinator and Admin can mute or unmute students.

Requirements:

- Add a Mute/Unmute action to the relevant student message menu.
- Add a `Muted` badge and Mute/Unmute action to the existing Staff → Students detail page.
- Update the existing profile record or equivalent user moderation record.
- Prevent staff from muting other staff members.
- Prevent students from changing their own mute status.
- Enforce permissions through the backend/database.
- Record the acting staff user and timestamp if the existing audit architecture supports it.
- Display clear success and error messages.

Do not change unrelated student profile information.

## 7. REAL-TIME ANNOUNCEMENT NOTIFICATIONS

When staff creates a new announcement:

1. Save the announcement successfully.
2. Generate notifications for eligible, approved students using the trusted backend.
3. Use the message format:

   `New announcement: <title>`

4. Link each notification to the Community page's announcements channel.
5. Update the existing notification bell and unread count.
6. Prevent duplicate notifications caused by retries or repeated requests.
7. Do not create notifications for unapproved accounts unless explicitly required by the existing authorization model.
8. Do not fabricate notifications or show success when notification creation fails.

Use the existing notification table and infrastructure.

Do not notify users before the announcement has been successfully saved.

## 8. STUDENT HOME — ANNOUNCEMENTS WIDGET

Add an `Announcements` section to the existing Student Home page.

Display a maximum of three announcements:

1. Pinned announcements first.
2. Remaining slots filled by the newest announcements.
3. Each item shows its title and publication date.
4. Each item links to the corresponding announcement in the Community page.
5. Fetch all content from the real backend.
6. Show a useful empty state if no announcements exist.

Do not create a duplicate Student Home page.

Preserve existing dashboard cards, internship progress, and report information.

## 9. UNREAD COMMUNITY INDICATOR

Add an unread dot to the existing Community sidebar item when there is new activity since the user last viewed the relevant channel.

Use the existing architecture or create a minimal `channel_reads` table if required.

Logical fields:

- `user_id`
- `channel`
- `last_seen_at`

Requirements:

- Store last-seen state per authenticated user and channel.
- Support `community` and `announcements`.
- Update last-seen state when the user opens the relevant channel.
- Clear the relevant unread indicator only after the appropriate channel has been opened and its latest content has been loaded successfully.
- Do not mark content as seen for other users.
- Use actual timestamps and database records.
- Prevent unauthorized users from reading or updating another user's channel-read state.
- Do not rely only on local storage for cross-device unread state.

If the current architecture has a suitable existing read-tracking mechanism, reuse it instead of creating duplicate tables.

## 10. DATABASE MIGRATIONS

Inspect the existing database before creating migrations.

Reuse existing tables wherever possible.

Ensure the data model supports the equivalent of:

### Messages

- `id`
- `sender_id`
- `channel`
- `content`
- `deleted`
- `deleted_by`
- `created_at`
- `updated_at`

### Announcements

- `id`
- `title`
- `body`
- `pinned`
- `created_by`
- `created_at`
- `updated_at`

### Profile Moderation

- Existing user/profile relationship
- `muted`, default false, if not already available

### Channel Reads

- `user_id`
- `channel`
- `last_seen_at`

Adapt names and relationships to the existing schema.

Use safe, additive, version-controlled migrations.

Do not recreate existing tables, erase existing data, or introduce duplicate fields.

Ensure the schema supports:

- Valid sender relationships
- Valid channel names
- Message length constraints
- Safe soft deletion
- Rate limiting
- Pinned announcement limits
- Appropriate foreign keys and indexes
- Authorized per-user read tracking

Enable real-time subscriptions only if supported by the actual backend and current configuration.

If using Django, use its existing migrations and backend conventions. If using Supabase, use its existing PostgreSQL migrations and security model. Do not mix architectures unnecessarily.

## 11. SECURITY AND AUTHORIZATION

Enforce security on the server/database. Frontend controls alone are insufficient.

### Read Permissions

- Approved users can read authorized, non-deleted community messages.
- Approved students and staff can read announcements according to the existing access rules.
- Users cannot access private data outside their authorization scope.

### Message Insert Permissions

- Approved, non-muted students can post in `community`.
- Authorized staff can post in `community`.
- Only authorized staff can create announcements.
- The sender identity must come from the authenticated server-side identity.
- Students cannot impersonate another sender.
- Students cannot send messages while muted.

### Message Update Permissions

- Users can soft-delete only their own messages.
- Authorized staff can soft-delete community messages.
- Users cannot edit existing message content through update requests.
- Users cannot change another user's message, sender ID, role, or moderation fields.

### Announcement Permissions

- Only authorized Coordinator/Admin users can create, edit, delete, pin, or unpin announcements.
- Students cannot bypass read-only permissions using direct API/database requests.
- The three-pinned-announcements limit must be enforced server-side.

### Mute Permissions

- Only authorized staff can mute/unmute students.
- Staff cannot mute other staff.
- Students cannot mute/unmute themselves.
- The backend must reject unauthorized attempts.

### Rate Limiting

- Enforce one message per five-second interval per authenticated user on the server.
- Handle concurrent requests safely.
- Do not rely solely on JavaScript timers.

### General Security

- Never expose service-role keys or other backend secrets in frontend code.
- Validate all incoming data on the server.
- Prevent XSS and open redirects.
- Protect existing Phase 1 role permissions.
- Preserve Phase 2 internship security and Phase 3 report security.
- Do not weaken existing authorization policies.

## 12. PRESERVE EXISTING WEBSITE DESIGN AND FUNCTIONALITY

This is an incremental feature implementation.

Do not:

- Rebuild the website.
- Replace the existing frontend framework or backend.
- Change authentication or registration flows.
- Delete genuine student or staff accounts.
- Remove existing internships, reports, review history, or legitimate notifications.
- Change unrelated database schemas.
- Remove existing dashboard cards or sidebar entries.
- Redesign existing pages unnecessarily.
- Replace real database queries with sample data.
- Introduce unrelated features.
- Start Phase 5.

Keep the existing logo, visual identity, layouts, and navigation.

Only make the changes needed for Phase 4.

## 13. ACCEPTANCE TESTS

Run the actual tests available and report every item as PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED.

Fix all resolvable failures.

1. Two authorized accounts in separate browsers see new community messages in real time.
2. Messages display the correct sender, role, time, and content.
3. URLs are safely clickable and message HTML is rendered as plain text.
4. Empty messages are rejected.
5. Messages exceeding 1,000 characters are rejected by the server.
6. Rapid-fire messages are rejected by server-side rate limiting.
7. A student can delete their own message but cannot delete another student's message.
8. Staff can delete authorized community messages.
9. Students cannot post announcements through the UI or direct API requests.
10. Staff can create, edit, delete, pin, and unpin announcements.
11. More than three pinned announcements cannot be created, including under concurrent requests.
12. Students receive notifications for new announcements.
13. Student Home shows the latest pinned/recent real announcements.
14. Staff can mute and unmute a student.
15. Muted students can read messages but cannot send them.
16. Students cannot unmute themselves through direct API/database requests.
17. Staff cannot mute other staff members.
18. The unread dot appears for new activity and clears correctly after viewing the relevant channel.
19. Load older messages works without duplicating or skipping records.
20. Empty and error states display correctly without dummy fallback data.
21. Existing Phase 0, 1, 2, and 3 features continue working.
22. Existing genuine database records remain intact.
23. No new mock records or hardcoded fake statistics are introduced.
24. Desktop and mobile layouts work without horizontal overflow.
25. TypeScript, lint, backend tests, and production build pass where available.

Do not mark a test PASS merely because the UI exists.

If external services, credentials, or separate test accounts are unavailable, report the test as BLOCKED and explain the exact verification needed.

## Phase 4 Prompt (Copy-Paste)

```
PHASE 4 — COMMUNITY CHAT AND ANNOUNCEMENTS

Build on top of Phases 0 to 3. Do NOT modify or break any existing feature. Only add the following and fill the existing "Community" pages (student and staff) and the Home announcements area.

A) DATABASE ADDITIONS (SQL migration, additive only)
- Add column "muted" boolean default false to profiles.
- Add column "deleted" boolean default false and "deleted_by" uuid nullable to messages (soft delete).
- Ensure announcements has: id, title, body, pinned (default false), created_by, created_at.
- Enable Supabase Realtime on the messages and announcements tables.

B) COMMUNITY PAGE (same layout for student and staff) — sidebar tab "Community"
1. Two channels as tabs: "#announcements" and "#community".
2. #community:
   - Realtime chat: new messages appear instantly without refresh (Supabase Realtime subscription).
   - Each message shows sender name, role badge (Student / Coordinator / Admin), time, and content.
   - URLs in messages are auto-linked and open in a new tab (rel="noopener noreferrer"). Render content as plain text, never as HTML (prevent XSS).
   - Input box with Send button (Enter to send, Shift+Enter for new line). Max 1000 characters, no empty messages, max 1 message per 5 seconds per user with a friendly message.
   - Load the latest 50 messages, with a "Load older messages" button. Auto-scroll to the newest message, unless the user has scrolled up.
   - A user can delete their own message; staff can delete any message. Deleted messages show "This message was deleted".
   - If the logged-in student is muted, replace the input box with "You are muted by a coordinator" (can still read).
3. #announcements:
   - Shows announcements newest first, pinned ones on top with a pin icon.
   - Students: read-only. Staff: "New Announcement" button with a form (title required, body required, "Pin this announcement" checkbox), plus Edit, Delete, and Pin/Unpin on each.
   - Max 3 pinned announcements at a time; show a clear error when exceeded.

C) STAFF MODERATION
1. In #community, staff see a "Mute" / "Unmute" option on each student's message menu. Muting updates profiles.muted. Staff cannot mute other staff.
2. Staff "Students" page: add a "Muted" badge and a Mute/Unmute action in the student detail page.

D) NOTIFICATIONS AND HOME
1. When staff posts a new announcement: create a notification for every approved student ("New announcement: <title>") linking to the Community page, #announcements tab.
2. Student Home: show a section "Announcements" with pinned ones first, then the latest, maximum 3 total, each linking to the Community page.
3. Community sidebar item shows an unread dot when there are new messages or announcements since the user last opened the page (store last_seen per user per channel in a small table "channel_reads": user_id, channel, last_seen_at).

E) SECURITY (RLS)
- Approved users can read non-deleted messages and all announcements.
- Insert into messages: channel "community" for any approved, non-muted user; channel "announcements" for staff only. The sender_id must equal the logged-in user.
- Update messages: a user may only soft-delete their own message; staff may soft-delete any message. Nobody can edit message content.
- Announcements: only staff can insert, update, delete.
- Only staff can change profiles.muted, and never for other staff. A student must not be able to un-mute themselves (enforce with RLS or a database function, not only in the UI).
- The rate limit (5 seconds) is enforced server-side with a database trigger or function, not only in the UI.

ACCEPTANCE CHECKLIST — report each item as PASS or FAIL and fix any FAIL
[ ] Two logged-in accounts in two browsers see each other's #community messages instantly
[ ] Links in messages are clickable; HTML typed in a message is shown as plain text
[ ] Empty message, a message over 1000 characters, and rapid-fire messages are blocked
[ ] A student can delete their own message but not someone else's; staff can delete any
[ ] Students cannot post in #announcements (UI hidden and RLS blocks it)
[ ] Staff can create, edit, delete, and pin announcements; more than 3 pinned is blocked
[ ] Students get a notification for a new announcement; Student Home shows announcements
[ ] Staff can mute a student; the muted student cannot send messages (RLS blocks it) but can read
[ ] A muted student cannot un-mute themselves
[ ] Unread dot appears for new activity and clears after opening Community
[ ] "Load older messages" works
[ ] Everything works properly on a mobile screen
```

```
- Approved users can read non-deleted messages and all announcements.
- Insert into messages: channel "community" for any approved, non-muted user; channel "announcements" for staff only. The sender_id must equal the logged-in user.
- Update messages: a user may only soft-delete their own message; staff may soft-delete any message. Nobody can edit message content.
- Announcements: only staff can insert, update, delete.
- Only staff can change profiles.muted, and never for other staff. A student must not be able to un-mute themselves (enforce with RLS or a database function, not only in the UI).
- The rate limit (5 seconds) is enforced server-side with a database trigger or function, not only in the UI.

ACCEPTANCE CHECKLIST — report each item as PASS or FAIL and fix any FAIL
[ ] Two logged-in accounts in two browsers see each other's #community messages instantly
[ ] Links in messages are clickable; HTML typed in a message is shown as plain text
[ ] Empty message, a message over 1000 characters, and rapid-fire messages are blocked
[ ] A student can delete their own message but not someone else's; staff can delete any
[ ] Students cannot post in #announcements (UI hidden and RLS blocks it)
[ ] Staff can create, edit, delete, and pin announcements; more than 3 pinned is blocked
[ ] Students get a notification for a new announcement; Student Home shows announcements
[ ] Staff can mute a student; the muted student cannot send messages (RLS blocks it) but can read
[ ] A muted student cannot un-mute themselves
[ ] Unread dot appears for new activity and clears after opening Community
[ ] "Load older messages" works
[ ] Everything works properly on a mobile screen
```

## तपासणी कशी करायची

| Step | कृती |
|---|---|
| 1 | दोन browsers मध्ये एक staff आणि एक student account उघडा |
| 2 | #community मध्ये दोन्हीकडून message पाठवा, instantly दिसतो का बघा |

# PHASE 3 — WEEKLY PROGRESS REPORTS, REVIEW & STUDENT MONITORING

## PROJECT
Internship Performance Tracking System (IPTS) / Career Growth Hub

Act as a senior full-stack engineer working directly in my existing project workspace.

Implement Phase 3 only: Weekly Progress Reports, Staff Review Workflow, Student Progress Tracking, Inactive Student Monitoring, and Report Notifications.

**Do not merely provide instructions or mockups. Implement the actual functionality in the existing codebase.**

## 1. MANDATORY PRE-IMPLEMENTATION INSPECTION

Before changing any code:

1. Inspect the complete existing project structure, routes, components, services, hooks, database migrations, Supabase configuration, and README.
2. Verify that Phase 0 (Setup + Database), Phase 1 (Authentication + Roles + Student Approval), and Phase 2 (Internship Management) are implemented and working.
3. Verify the existing `profiles`, `user_roles`, `internships`, `student_internships`, and `notifications` schemas.
4. Inspect the current Student and Staff dashboards, sidebar navigation, shared layouts, and notification components.
5. Identify the existing Student, Coordinator, and Admin role permissions.
6. Reuse existing tables, services, types, layouts, and components wherever possible.
7. Do not recreate existing tables, authentication systems, dashboards, or notification infrastructure.
8. Check whether `weekly_reports` or an equivalent reports table already exists before creating anything.
9. If Phase 2 is incomplete or broken, document the blockers and do not proceed with unrelated architectural changes.
10. Preserve all existing data and functionality.

Do not start Phase 4.

## 2. TECHNOLOGY AND IMPLEMENTATION RULES

Preserve the existing technology stack. If already configured, continue using:

- React + Vite + TypeScript
- Existing Tailwind CSS and UI component library
- Supabase Auth
- PostgreSQL
- Supabase Row Level Security (RLS)
- Existing React Router configuration
- Existing toast, dialog, form validation, and notification components

Do not introduce unnecessary dependencies.

Use real database records. Do not use mock data, hardcoded counts, or fabricated progress statistics.

Create version-controlled, incremental SQL migrations. Never reset the database or delete existing records to make migrations pass.

## 3. STUDENT SIDE — WEEKLY REPORTS

Complete the existing Student Dashboard → Weekly Reports page.

Use the existing route if one exists. Otherwise, add:

`/student/weekly-reports`

### A. New Report Form

Create a simple, mobile-friendly `New Report` form with these fields:

| Field | Input | Required |
|---|---|---|
| Internship | Dropdown of the student's Ongoing internships | Yes |
| Week No. | Positive integer | Yes |
| What I Learned | Multiline text | Yes |
| Tools / Technologies Used | Tag input | Yes |
| Tasks Completed | Multiline text | Yes |
| Challenges | Multiline text | No |
| Next Week Plan | Multiline text | Yes |
| Hours Worked | Number, 0–80 | Yes |
| Proof Links | Multiple URLs | No |

### Internship Selection

- Only show internships associated with the authenticated student whose status is `Ongoing`.
- Use the actual `student_internships` records and existing relationships.
- If the student has no Ongoing internship, show a friendly message explaining how to mark an internship as Ongoing before submitting a report.
- Provide a navigation link to the existing internship status page when appropriate.
- Never allow a student to submit a report against another student's internship record.

### Validation

- Trim required text fields.
- Require a valid positive integer for Week No.
- Reject duplicate week numbers for the same student and internship.
- Enforce the duplicate rule in the database using a unique constraint or an equivalent safe mechanism.
- Require at least one non-empty tools/technologies tag.
- Validate Hours Worked between 0 and 80, inclusive.
- Validate proof links as legitimate HTTP/HTTPS URLs.
- Reject `javascript:`, `data:`, and unsupported URL schemes.
- Validate every supplied proof link individually.
- Show field-specific error messages.
- Prevent duplicate form submissions.
- Show loading indicators and success/error feedback.
- Persist all submitted data in Supabase.

Do not rely on frontend validation alone.

### Week Number Rule

A student must not submit multiple reports for the same week of the same internship.

Use the unique combination of the actual student-internship relationship and `week_number`, or the equivalent existing schema fields.

If the unique constraint is violated, show a clear message such as:

`A report for this internship and week number already exists.`

Do not silently overwrite another report.

## 4. STUDENT — MY REPORTS LIST

Display the authenticated student's reports, newest first.

Each row or card must include:

- Internship name
- Week number
- Submission date
- Hours worked
- Status badge
- Coordinator comment, if present
- View Details action

Supported report statuses:

- `Pending` — yellow
- `Approved` — green
- `Needs Improvement` — red

Use the existing design system and consistent status labels.

### Report Details

Clicking a report must open its complete detail view, including:

- Internship
- Week number
- Learned
- Tools and technologies
- Tasks completed
- Challenges
- Next week plan
- Hours worked
- Proof links
- Submission and update timestamps
- Current status
- Coordinator review comment

Students must only be able to access their own reports.

### Edit and Resubmit

- A `Pending` report cannot be edited or resubmitted while awaiting review.
- An `Approved` report is permanently read-only to the student.
- A `Needs Improvement` report can be edited and resubmitted.
- Resubmission must change its status back to `Pending`.
- Resubmission must preserve the existing report identity and history where supported.
- Clear or supersede the previous review comment appropriately without destroying useful audit history.
- Notify staff about the resubmission.
- Prevent students from changing their own status or coordinator comment.

Do not allow an ordinary student to bypass these rules through direct database requests.

## 5. STUDENT — PROGRESS SUMMARY

Add a progress summary to the Weekly Reports page.

Show:

1. Total reports submitted
2. Total approved reports
3. Total hours worked
4. Current weekly reporting streak
5. Progress percentage for each relevant ongoing internship

All figures must be calculated from real database records.

### Progress Percentage

For each internship:

`Progress % = min(100, approved reports / expected reports × 100)`

Expected reports are calculated from the internship's recorded `start_date` to the current date, with a minimum of one expected report.

Implementation details:

- Use the actual internship start date from the existing data model.
- Calculate elapsed weeks consistently, using the project's agreed week-counting convention.
- Do not divide by zero.
- Cap progress at 100%.
- Count only reports with status `Approved` in the numerator.
- Exclude pending and needs-improvement reports from approved progress.
- If the required start date is missing, use a clearly documented safe fallback and do not invent an internship start date.
- Calculate dates consistently and avoid off-by-one errors.

### Current Weekly Reporting Streak

Calculate consecutive weeks with at least one submitted report for the same internship.

- Use actual submission timestamps and week numbers where available.
- Do not count multiple reports from the same week as multiple streak weeks.
- Do not count future weeks.
- Reset the streak when a week is missed.
- Clearly document the rule used to identify the current week and the most recent reporting week.

Keep the calculation deterministic and test it against boundary dates.

## 6. STUDENT HOME — MY PROGRESS CARD

Add a `My Progress` card to the existing Student Home dashboard.

Display:

- Overall progress percentage across relevant ongoing internships
- Approved report count
- Pending report count
- Last report status
- Latest submission date
- A link to Weekly Reports

Define overall progress using the actual internship-level progress calculations and document the aggregation method. Avoid allowing an internship with many expected weeks to distort the result unintentionally.

If no ongoing internships or reports exist, show a useful empty state.

Do not create a second Student Dashboard or duplicate the home route.

## 7. STAFF SIDE — REPORT REVIEWS

Complete the existing Staff Dashboard → Report Reviews page for both Coordinator and Admin.

Use the existing staff route if available. Otherwise, add:

`/staff/report-reviews`

### A. Reports Table

Display actual reports from Supabase.

Columns:

- Student Name
- PRN / Student ID
- Internship
- Week Number
- Submitted Date
- Hours Worked
- Report Status
- Actions

Provide filters for:

- Status — default to Pending
- Internship
- Branch / Department
- Academic Year
- Search by student name or PRN

Include loading, empty, error, and pagination states where appropriate.

Staff must be able to access all report records necessary for their authorized responsibilities.

### B. Report Review Detail

Clicking a report opens its full detail view.

Display all submitted fields, proof links, student details required for review, submission timestamps, and previous review information when available.

Provide a review panel containing:

- `Approve` action
- `Needs Improvement` action
- Coordinator comment field

### Review Rules

**Approve:**

- Update the report status to `Approved`.
- Save the reviewing staff user's ID and review timestamp if the schema supports them.
- Save an optional comment if supplied.
- Notify the report owner.
- Update student progress calculations using the newly approved report.

**Needs Improvement:**

- Require a non-empty coordinator comment.
- Trim whitespace and reject an empty comment.
- Update the status to `Needs Improvement`.
- Save the comment, reviewer ID, and review timestamp where supported.
- Notify the report owner.
- Allow the student to edit and resubmit the report.

Additional rules:

- Only authorized Coordinator/Admin users can review reports.
- Prevent accidental double reviews and stale updates.
- Disable review actions while a request is processing.
- Handle database failures without showing false success messages.
- Use the database as the source of truth.
- Never let a student approve their own report.
- Prevent unauthorized status changes using RLS or secure database functions.

`/staff/inactive-students`

### Definition

A student is inactive for this reporting workflow when:

- The student has at least one associated internship with status `Ongoing`.

Display:

- Student Name
- PRN / Student ID
- Branch / Department
- Academic Year
- Ongoing Internship
- Last Report Date
- Days Inactive

### Calculation Rules

- Use actual report submission timestamps.
- Use a consistent timezone for the 14-day comparison.
- Include students who have never submitted a report for the relevant ongoing internship.
- For students with multiple ongoing internships, evaluate each student-internship relationship separately.
- Avoid duplicate rows for the same student-internship relationship.
- If no report exists, display `Never submitted` and calculate inactivity from a documented reference date, such as the internship start date, only when that date is available.
- Do not silently treat missing dates as verified inactivity.
- Recalculate the list from current database records.

Provide useful empty, loading, and error states.

## 13. ROW LEVEL SECURITY — CRITICAL

Enforce all permissions in the database. Frontend hiding is not sufficient.

Review the existing RLS policies before adding or modifying policies.

### Student Report Access

Students may:

- Read only their own reports.
- Insert reports only for their own valid `Ongoing` student-internship relationships.
- Update only their own reports when their status is `Needs Improvement`.
- Resubmit an eligible report with status returning to `Pending`.

Students must not:

- Read another student's reports.
- Change their `student_internship_id` to access another student's internship.
- Change `status` directly.
- Change `coordinator_comment`.
- Set `reviewed_by` or `reviewed_at`.
- Edit an Approved report.
- Bypass the unique week constraint.
- Send notifications to arbitrary users.

Enforce protected-field restrictions through appropriate database policies, triggers, or secure functions.

### Staff Report Access

Authorized Coordinator/Admin users may:

- Read all weekly reports required for their responsibilities.
- Review and update report status.
- Add coordinator comments.
- Access associated student and internship information needed for review.

Only authorized staff may perform privileged review operations.

### Security Implementation

- Use `auth.uid()` or the equivalent trusted authenticated identity.
- Do not trust a browser-supplied user ID.
- Do not expose Supabase service-role keys in client-side code.
- Avoid recursive RLS policies.
- Restrict security-definer functions with explicit permissions and a safe `search_path`.
- Ensure notification triggers cannot be abused to create arbitrary cross-user notifications.
- Preserve existing Phase 1 and Phase 2 RLS behavior.
- Test policies using separate Student and Staff accounts and direct database/API requests where possible.

If a security rule cannot be verified, report it as BLOCKED rather than claiming success.

## 3. STUDENT SIDE — WEEKLY REPORTS

Complete the existing Student Dashboard → Weekly Reports page.

Use the existing route if one exists. Otherwise, add:

`/student/weekly-reports`

### A. New Report Form

Create a simple, mobile-friendly `New Report` form with these fields:

| Field | Input | Required |
|---|---|---|
| Internship | Dropdown of the student's Ongoing internships | Yes |
| Week No. | Positive integer | Yes |
| What I Learned | Multiline text | Yes |
| Tools / Technologies Used | Tag input | Yes |
| Tasks Completed | Multiline text | Yes |
| Challenges | Multiline text | No |
| Next Week Plan | Multiline text | Yes |
| Hours Worked | Number, 0–80 | Yes |
| Proof Links | Multiple URLs | No |

### Internship Selection

- Only show internships associated with the authenticated student whose status is `Ongoing`.
- Use the actual `student_internships` records and existing relationships.
- If the student has no Ongoing internship, show a friendly message explaining how to mark an internship as Ongoing before submitting a report.
- Provide a navigation link to the existing internship status page when appropriate.
- Never allow a student to submit a report against another student's internship record.

### Validation

- Trim required text fields.
- Require a valid positive integer for Week No.
- Reject duplicate week numbers for the same student and internship.
- Enforce the duplicate rule in the database using a unique constraint or an equivalent safe mechanism.
- Require at least one non-empty tools/technologies tag.
- Validate Hours Worked between 0 and 80, inclusive.
- Validate proof links as legitimate HTTP/HTTPS URLs.
- Reject `javascript:`, `data:`, and unsupported URL schemes.
- Validate every supplied proof link individually.
- Show field-specific error messages.
- Prevent duplicate form submissions.
- Show loading indicators and success/error feedback.
- Persist all submitted data in Supabase.

Do not rely on frontend validation alone.

### Week Number Rule

A student must not submit multiple reports for the same week of the same internship.

Use the unique combination of the actual student-internship relationship and `week_number`, or the equivalent existing schema fields.

If the unique constraint is violated, show a clear message such as:

`A report for this internship and week number already exists.`

Do not silently overwrite another report.

- Internship

- Tools and technologies
- Tasks completed
- Challenges
- Next week plan
- Hours worked

- Current status
- Coordinator review comment

Students must only be able to access their own reports.

### Edit and Resubmit

- A `Pending` report cannot be edited or resubmitted while awaiting review.
- An `Approved` report is permanently read-only to the student.
- A `Needs Improvement` report can be edited and resubmitted.
- Resubmission must change its status back to `Pending`.

- Notify staff about the resubmission.
- Prevent students from changing their own status or coordinator comment.

Do not allow an ordinary student to bypass these rules through direct database requests.

## 5. STUDENT — PROGRESS SUMMARY

Add a progress summary to the Weekly Reports page.

Show:

1. Total reports submitted
2. Total approved reports
3. Total hours worked
4. Current weekly reporting streak
5. Progress percentage for each relevant ongoing internship

All figures must be calculated from real database records.

### Progress Percentage

For each internship:

`Progress % = min(100, approved reports / expected reports × 100)`

Expected reports are calculated from the internship's recorded `start_date` to the current date, with a minimum of one expected report.

Implementation details:

- Use the actual internship start date from the existing data model.
- Calculate elapsed weeks consistently, using the project's agreed week-counting convention.
- Do not divide by zero.
- Cap progress at 100%.
- Count only reports with status `Approved` in the numerator.
- Exclude pending and needs-improvement reports from approved progress.
- If the required start date is missing, use a clearly documented safe fallback and do not invent an internship start date.
- Calculate dates consistently and avoid off-by-one errors.

### Current Weekly Reporting Streak

Calculate consecutive weeks with at least one submitted report for the same internship.

- Use actual submission timestamps and week numbers where available.
- Do not count multiple reports from the same week as multiple streak weeks.
- Do not count future weeks.
- Reset the streak when a week is missed.
- Clearly document the rule used to identify the current week and the most recent reporting week.

Keep the calculation deterministic and test it against boundary dates.

### Progress Percentage

`Progress % = min(100, approved reports / expected reports × 100)`

Expected reports are calculated from the internship's recorded `start_date` to the current date, with a minimum of one expected report.

- If the required start date is missing, use a clearly documented safe fallback and do not invent an internship start date.
- Calculate dates consistently and avoid off-by-one errors.

Calculate consecutive weeks with at least one submitted report for the same internship.

- Do not count multiple reports from the same week as multiple streak weeks.
- Do not count future weeks.
- Reset the streak when a week is missed.
