:::writing{variant="document" id="61482"}
# PHASE 1 — AUTHENTICATION + ROLES + STUDENT APPROVAL

## Project: Internship Performance Tracking System (IPTS)

You are a senior full-stack developer working on an existing Internship Performance Tracking System.

Phase 0 (Project Setup and Database) has already been completed. Your task is to implement Phase 1: Authentication, Role-Based Access Control, Student Registration Approval, and protected dashboards.

**IMPORTANT:** Implement the actual code in the existing workspace. Do not merely explain the implementation.

---

## 1. FIRST: INSPECT THE EXISTING PROJECT

Before changing anything:

1. Inspect the current folder structure and existing code.
2. Read the existing README, environment configuration, database migrations, Supabase client, profiles table, and user_roles table.
3. Verify which authentication and authorization features already exist.
4. Reuse the existing database schema and components wherever possible.
5. Do not recreate existing tables or create duplicate authentication systems.
6. Do not delete or replace working functionality from Phase 0.
7. Create a short implementation plan and then proceed.

If Supabase credentials or configuration are missing, implement the code and document the required configuration. Do not pretend that live authentication has been tested.

## 2. TECHNOLOGY STACK

Preserve the existing stack. For a new or already configured Phase 0 project, use:

- React.js
- Vite
- TypeScript
- Tailwind CSS
- shadcn/ui where appropriate
- Supabase Auth
- Supabase PostgreSQL
- Supabase Row Level Security (RLS)
- React Router, if routing is not already implemented
- React Hook Form and Zod, if useful for form validation
- Lucide React icons

Use the existing Supabase client rather than creating multiple clients.

## 3. USER ROLES

Implement three application roles.

### A. Student

A registered student can:

- Sign up with their college information.
- Sign in after approval.
- View their own Student Dashboard.
- View and edit permitted personal profile fields.
- View their account approval status.
- Sign out securely.

A student must never be able to access staff pages or staff-only APIs.

### B. Coordinator

A coordinator can:

- Sign in to the Staff Dashboard.
- Access authorized staff routes.
- View the staff dashboard shell.
- Sign out securely.

The Coordinator role will be granted only through an authorized administrative process.

### C. Admin

An admin can:

- Sign in to the same Staff Dashboard used by Coordinators.
- Access authorized staff routes.
- Access administrative controls reserved for Admins.
- Sign out securely.

Admin-only staff management features will be implemented in the appropriate later phase.

**Important:** Coordinator and Admin share the same dashboard shell, but their permissions must remain distinct. A Coordinator must not be able to perform Admin-only operations.

## 4. AUTHENTICATION PAGES

Create the following pages with a consistent, professional design.

### A. Login Page — `/login`

Fields:

- Email
- Password
- Show/hide password control
- Remember session option only if compatible with the configured Supabase session behavior
- Sign In button
- Forgot Password link
- Link to Student Registration

Requirements:

- Validate email format.
- Require a password.
- Display clear validation and authentication errors.
- Show a loading state while submitting.
- Prevent accidental duplicate submissions.
- Never log passwords or expose them in error messages.
- Do not reveal whether a particular email belongs to an existing account.
- After successful authentication, retrieve the user's role and approval status from trusted database records.

Redirect users as follows:

- Approved Student → `/student/dashboard`
- Coordinator → `/staff/dashboard`
- Admin → `/staff/dashboard`
- Pending Student → `/pending-approval`
- Rejected Student → `/account-status`

Do not rely on a user-selected role or untrusted user metadata for redirection or authorization.

### B. Student Registration Page — `/register`

Create a registration form with these fields:

- Full Name — required
- College Email — required
- Password — required
- Confirm Password — required
- PRN / Student ID — required
- Department / Branch — required
- Academic Year — required
- Skills — optional
- Agree to Privacy Policy — required

Requirements:

1. Validate all required fields.
2. Confirm that both passwords match.
3. Enforce reasonable password-strength requirements.
4. Display clear validation messages.
5. Do not store passwords in the profiles table.
6. Use Supabase Auth for account creation.
7. Create the corresponding profile securely using the existing database-side profile creation mechanism where available.
8. Set new student accounts to `pending` approval.
9. Assign only the `student` role through a trusted process.
10. Never accept `admin` or `coordinator` as a registration role.
11. Handle duplicate email, duplicate PRN, email verification, and database errors gracefully.
12. Do not create duplicate profiles if a profile already exists.

After registration:

- Show a registration-success page or message.
- Explain that the account requires staff approval.
- If email verification is enabled, instruct the student to verify their email.
- Do not grant dashboard access until both the applicable email-verification requirement and account-approval requirement are satisfied.

If Supabase email confirmation is enabled, handle the state where the user has registered but does not yet have a valid authenticated session.

### C. Forgot Password — `/forgot-password`

Implement the password-reset request flow using Supabase Auth.

Requirements:

- Accept an email address.
- Use the official Supabase password recovery method.
- Show a generic success message that does not reveal whether the account exists.
- Do not send passwords through email.
- Handle rate limits and configuration errors safely.

### D. Reset Password — `/reset-password`

Implement the recovery flow using Supabase-supported recovery sessions.

Requirements:

- Verify that the recovery session is valid.
- Allow the user to enter and confirm a new password.
- Validate password strength.
- Update the password through Supabase Auth.
- Show a success message and provide a link to sign in.
- Never allow password changes by directly editing the profiles table.

## 5. ACCOUNT APPROVAL SYSTEM

Use the existing `profiles.approval_status` field from Phase 0.

Supported values:

- `pending`
- `approved`
- `rejected`

Create the following page.

### `/pending-approval`

Display a professional status page for students waiting for approval.

Show:

- A pending approval message.
- The student's registration email.
- A short explanation that college staff must approve the account.
- A Refresh Status button.
- A Sign Out button.

When the student refreshes the status or the session is revalidated, retrieve the current approval status securely.

If approved, redirect to `/student/dashboard`.

If rejected, redirect to `/account-status`.

Do not allow a pending student to access protected student pages merely by entering a URL.

### `/account-status`

Show a clear message when an account is rejected.

Include:

- A generic account-status explanation.
- A contact-support instruction.
- A Sign Out button.

Do not expose private administrative comments or internal approval notes.

## 6. PROTECTED ROUTES AND ROLE-BASED ACCESS

Implement reusable route protection.

Suggested components:

- `AuthProvider`
- `ProtectedRoute`
- `RoleGuard`
- `StudentRoute`
- `StaffRoute`
- `AdminRoute`

Reuse existing equivalents if present.

### Public routes

- `/`
- `/login`
- `/register`
- `/forgot-password`
- `/reset-password`

### Student routes

- `/student/dashboard`
- `/student/profile`

Allow access only to authenticated, email-verified users when verification is enabled, with the `student` role and approved account status.

### Staff routes

- `/staff/dashboard`

Allow access only to authenticated users with a valid `coordinator` or `admin` role and the appropriate account permissions.

### Admin routes

- `/staff/manage-staff`

Reserve this route for the Admin role. It may display a clearly labelled placeholder in Phase 1; full staff management will be implemented later.

### Other routes

- `/pending-approval`
- `/account-status`
- A branded Not Found page

Security requirements:

1. Unauthenticated users accessing protected pages must be redirected to `/login`.
2. Approved students accessing staff pages must be denied and redirected to their Student Dashboard.
3. Pending students must not access either dashboard.
4. Rejected students must not access either dashboard.
5. Coordinators must not access Admin-only routes.
6. Invalid or missing role data must fail closed.
7. Never rely on hiding sidebar items as the only access control.
8. Enforce permissions at the database and server boundaries using RLS and trusted backend operations.
9. Recheck authorization when the session changes or the user returns to the application.
10. Handle expired sessions and revoked permissions safely.

## 7. SECURE ROLE MANAGEMENT

Use the existing `user_roles` table.

Requirements:

- Students receive only the Student role through the trusted registration process.
- Registration requests must never grant Coordinator or Admin permissions.
- Do not use editable profile fields or user-controlled metadata as the source of authorization.
- Do not expose a service-role key to the browser.
- Privileged role assignment must use a trusted administrative process.
- Prevent users from modifying their own role assignments.
- Ensure that role checks cannot be bypassed by changing browser state, local storage, or frontend requests.

If the existing Phase 0 database schema does not enforce these rules, create a safe, version-controlled migration to correct the issue without destroying existing data.

## 8. INITIAL STUDENT DASHBOARD

Create a functional but minimal Student Dashboard.

Route: `/student/dashboard`

Display:

- Welcome message using the authenticated user's profile name.
- Account status.
- Department and academic year.
- Profile completion information, if calculated from real profile fields.
- Navigation to My Profile.
- A placeholder section for future Internship Opportunities.
- A placeholder section for future Weekly Progress Reports.
- Sign Out.

Do not show fabricated internship counts, progress percentages, student rankings, or application statistics.

### Student Profile — `/student/profile`

Allow students to view and update permitted fields:

- Full Name
- Department
- Academic Year
- Skills
- Bio
- Avatar, only if profile image storage is configured

Students must not be able to modify:

- Application role
- Approval status
- Administrative permissions
- Another user's profile

Validate all updates and enforce the same restrictions in the database.

## 9. INITIAL STAFF DASHBOARD

Create one shared dashboard shell for Coordinator and Admin.

Route: `/staff/dashboard`

Display:

- Welcome message.
- Current user's name and role.
- A clean sidebar.
- Navigation placeholders for future modules:
  - Overview
  - Internships
  - Students
  - Report Reviews
  - Community
  - Approvals
  - Export
  - Manage Staff

Show `Manage Staff` only to Admins.

Other future modules may display a clear “Coming in a later phase” state. Do not implement their full functionality in Phase 1.

Include a working Sign Out button.

Do not display fabricated statistics or pretend that future modules are already functional.

## 10. STAFF APPROVAL PREPARATION

The existing `profiles.approval_status` field must be ready for future staff approval workflows.

In Phase 1:

- Ensure the database supports pending, approved, and rejected states.
- Ensure only authorized staff can change approval status through a trusted process.
- Ensure students cannot approve themselves.
- Do not implement the full Approvals management table unless the existing project already contains a working version.
- Do not create a public endpoint that lets anyone approve accounts.
- Document the secure administrative procedure needed to approve the initial student account.

For initial Admin bootstrap, use a trusted, documented procedure executed by an authorized project owner. Never allow public registration to create an Admin.

## 11. DATABASE AND RLS REVIEW

Inspect existing Supabase RLS policies and migrations.

Verify or safely add policies for:

- Profile ownership.
- Trusted role lookup.
- Student account approval.
- Student access restrictions.
- Staff-only protected operations.
- Admin-only role management.
- Authenticated user isolation.

Important:

- A user's ability to sign in must not automatically grant access to protected data.
- Pending and rejected accounts must not be treated as approved users.
- Students may update permitted profile fields but must not change protected role or approval fields.
- Students must not read private profiles or records belonging to other students.
- Coordinator/Admin access must be enforced by trusted role checks.
- Avoid recursive RLS policies.
- If a security-definer helper is needed, use a safe search path and restrict execution permissions.
- Ensure no policy allows a user to insert an Admin role for themselves.
- Keep all schema changes version-controlled.

Do not claim RLS has been verified against a live database unless the migrations and tests have actually been executed.

## 12. UI AND USER EXPERIENCE

Use a clean, professional, modern college career-platform design.

Requirements:

- Responsive mobile, tablet, and desktop layouts.
- Consistent typography, spacing, buttons, and form fields.
- Accessible form labels and keyboard navigation.
- Visible validation errors.
- Loading indicators.
- Empty states.
- Success and error notifications.
- Confirmation before signing out if there are unsaved changes.
- No unnecessary animations.
- No broken links or dead buttons.
- No fake user data.

Use a shared layout for authentication pages and separate protected layouts for Student and Staff dashboards.

## 13. ERROR HANDLING

Handle these scenarios:

- Invalid email or password.
- Unverified email.
- Pending or rejected student.
- Missing profile.
- Missing or invalid role.
- Expired session.
- Password reset errors.
- Duplicate PRN.
- Supabase connection failure.
- Database permission errors.
- Unexpected application errors.

Show user-friendly messages while keeping sensitive implementation details out of the interface.

Log only safe diagnostic information. Never log passwords, authentication tokens, secret keys, or sensitive personal data.

## 14. TESTING AND VERIFICATION

Run available automated checks, TypeScript validation, linting, and production build.

Test the following scenarios:

1. A new student can register.
2. The new student receives the correct pending approval state.
3. A pending student cannot open `/student/dashboard`.
4. A pending student cannot open `/staff/dashboard`.
5. An approved student can open the Student Dashboard.
6. An approved student cannot open Staff or Admin routes.
7. A Coordinator can open `/staff/dashboard`.
8. A Coordinator cannot open Admin-only routes.
9. An Admin can open `/staff/dashboard`.
10. An Admin can access the reserved staff-management route.
11. An unauthenticated user cannot access protected pages.
12. A rejected student cannot access either dashboard.
13. A student cannot change their own role or approval status.
14. A user cannot modify another user's private profile.
15. Sign Out clears the authenticated session.
16. Password recovery works when the required Supabase configuration is available.
17. The UI works on mobile screens.
18. Existing Phase 0 functionality remains intact.

Use automated tests where practical. For RLS, test with separate authenticated accounts or appropriate database-level test fixtures. Do not rely solely on frontend navigation tests.

Fix all failures that can be resolved within Phase 1.

If credentials, email configuration, or live database access are unavailable, mark the affected checks as BLOCKED rather than PASS.

## 15. SCOPE RESTRICTIONS

Implement Phase 1 only.

Do not implement:

- Internship creation or publishing.
- Internship application tracking.
- Weekly progress reports.
- Report approval workflows.
- Community chat.
- Resume generation.
- Excel/PDF exports.
- Inactive student detection.
- Leaderboards.
- International opportunity management.

These will be added in later phases.

## 16. DEFINITION OF DONE

Phase 1 is complete when:

- Registration and login interfaces work.
- Password recovery is implemented.
- Student approval status is enforced.
- Student, Coordinator, and Admin roles are handled securely.
- Student and Staff dashboards use the correct protected routes.
- Admin-only routes are restricted.
- Database policies prevent privilege escalation.
- Existing Phase 0 functionality is preserved.

- The README contains updated setup and testing instructions.

# PHASE 1 — AUTHENTICATION + ROLES + STUDENT APPROVAL

## Project: Internship Performance Tracking System (IPTS)

You are a senior full-stack developer working on an existing Internship Performance Tracking System.

Phase 0 (Project Setup and Database) has already been completed. Your task is to implement Phase 1: Authentication, Role-Based Access Control, Student Registration Approval, and protected dashboards.

**IMPORTANT:** Implement the actual code in the existing workspace. Do not merely explain the implementation.

---

## 1. FIRST: INSPECT THE EXISTING PROJECT

Before changing anything:

1. Inspect the current folder structure and existing code.
2. Read the existing README, environment configuration, database migrations, Supabase client, profiles table, and user_roles table.
3. Verify which authentication and authorization features already exist.
4. Reuse the existing database schema and components wherever possible.
5. Do not recreate existing tables or create duplicate authentication systems.
6. Do not delete or replace working functionality from Phase 0.
7. Create a short implementation plan and then proceed.

If Supabase credentials or configuration are missing, implement the code and document the required configuration. Do not pretend that live authentication has been tested.

## 2. TECHNOLOGY STACK

Preserve the existing stack. For a new or already configured Phase 0 project, use:

- React.js
- Vite
- TypeScript
- Tailwind CSS
- shadcn/ui where appropriate
- Supabase Auth
- Supabase PostgreSQL
- Supabase Row Level Security (RLS)
- React Router, if routing is not already implemented
- React Hook Form and Zod, if useful for form validation
- Lucide React icons

Use the existing Supabase client rather than creating multiple clients.

## 3. USER ROLES

Implement three application roles.

### A. Student

A registered student can:

- Sign up with their college information.
- Sign in after approval.
- View their own Student Dashboard.
- View and edit permitted personal profile fields.
- View their account approval status.
- Sign out securely.

A student must never be able to access staff pages or staff-only APIs.

### B. Coordinator

A coordinator can:

- Sign in to the Staff Dashboard.
- Access authorized staff routes.
- View the staff dashboard shell.
- Sign out securely.

The Coordinator role will be granted only through an authorized administrative process.

### C. Admin

An admin can:

- Sign in to the same Staff Dashboard used by Coordinators.
- Access authorized staff routes.
- Access administrative controls reserved for Admins.
- Sign out securely.

Admin-only staff management features will be implemented in the appropriate later phase.

**Important:** Coordinator and Admin share the same dashboard shell, but their permissions must remain distinct. A Coordinator must not be able to perform Admin-only operations.

## 4. AUTHENTICATION PAGES

Create the following pages with a consistent, professional design.

### A. Login Page — `/login`

Fields:

- Email
- Password
- Show/hide password control
- Remember session option only if compatible with the configured Supabase session behavior
- Sign In button
- Forgot Password link
- Link to Student Registration

Requirements:

- Validate email format.
- Require a password.
- Display clear validation and authentication errors.
- Show a loading state while submitting.
- Prevent accidental duplicate submissions.
- Never log passwords or expose them in error messages.
- Do not reveal whether a particular email belongs to an existing account.
- After successful authentication, retrieve the user's role and approval status from trusted database records.

Redirect users as follows:

- Approved Student → `/student/dashboard`
- Coordinator → `/staff/dashboard`
- Admin → `/staff/dashboard`
- Pending Student → `/pending-approval`
- Rejected Student → `/account-status`

Do not rely on a user-selected role or untrusted user metadata for redirection or authorization.

### B. Student Registration Page — `/register`

Create a registration form with these fields:

- Full Name — required
- College Email — required
- Password — required
- Confirm Password — required
- PRN / Student ID — required
- Department / Branch — required
- Academic Year — required
- Skills — optional
- Agree to Privacy Policy — required

Requirements:

1. Validate all required fields.
2. Confirm that both passwords match.
3. Enforce reasonable password-strength requirements.
4. Display clear validation messages.
5. Do not store passwords in the profiles table.
6. Use Supabase Auth for account creation.
7. Create the corresponding profile securely using the existing database-side profile creation mechanism where available.
8. Set new student accounts to `pending` approval.
9. Assign only the `student` role through a trusted process.
10. Never accept `admin` or `coordinator` as a registration role.
11. Handle duplicate email, duplicate PRN, email verification, and database errors gracefully.
12. Do not create duplicate profiles if a profile already exists.

After registration:

- Show a registration-success page or message.
- Explain that the account requires staff approval.
- If email verification is enabled, instruct the student to verify their email.
- Do not grant dashboard access until both the applicable email-verification requirement and account-approval requirement are satisfied.

If Supabase email confirmation is enabled, handle the state where the user has registered but does not yet have a valid authenticated session.

### C. Forgot Password — `/forgot-password`

Implement the password-reset request flow using Supabase Auth.

Requirements:

- Accept an email address.
- Use the official Supabase password recovery method.
- Show a generic success message that does not reveal whether the account exists.
- Do not send passwords through email.
- Handle rate limits and configuration errors safely.

### D. Reset Password — `/reset-password`

Implement the recovery flow using Supabase-supported recovery sessions.

Requirements:

- Verify that the recovery session is valid.
- Allow the user to enter and confirm a new password.
- Validate password strength.
- Update the password through Supabase Auth.
- Show a success message and provide a link to sign in.
- Never allow password changes by directly editing the profiles table.

## 5. ACCOUNT APPROVAL SYSTEM

Use the existing `profiles.approval_status` field from Phase 0.

Supported values:

- `pending`
- `approved`
- `rejected`

Create the following page.

### `/pending-approval`

Display a professional status page for students waiting for approval.

Show:

- A pending approval message.
- The student's registration email.
- A short explanation that college staff must approve the account.
- A Refresh Status button.
- A Sign Out button.

When the student refreshes the status or the session is revalidated, retrieve the current approval status securely.

If approved, redirect to `/student/dashboard`.

If rejected, redirect to `/account-status`.

Do not allow a pending student to access protected student pages merely by entering a URL.

### `/account-status`

Show a clear message when an account is rejected.

Include:

- A generic account-status explanation.
- A contact-support instruction.
- A Sign Out button.

Do not expose private administrative comments or internal approval notes.

## 6. PROTECTED ROUTES AND ROLE-BASED ACCESS

Suggested components:

- `AuthProvider`
- `ProtectedRoute`
- `RoleGuard`

- `StaffRoute`
- `AdminRoute`

- `/register`

- `/reset-password`

### Student routes

### Staff routes

- `/staff/dashboard`

Allow access only to authenticated users with a valid `coordinator` or `admin` role and the appropriate account permissions.

### Admin routes

- `/staff/manage-staff`

Reserve this route for the Admin role. It may display a clearly labelled placeholder in Phase 1; full staff management will be implemented later.

### Other routes

- `/pending-approval`
- `/account-status`
- A branded Not Found page

Security requirements:

1. Unauthenticated users accessing protected pages must be redirected to `/login`.
2. Approved students accessing staff pages must be denied and redirected to their Student Dashboard.
3. Pending students must not access either dashboard.
4. Rejected students must not access either dashboard.
5. Coordinators must not access Admin-only routes.
6. Invalid or missing role data must fail closed.
7. Never rely on hiding sidebar items as the only access control.
8. Enforce permissions at the database and server boundaries using RLS and trusted backend operations.
9. Recheck authorization when the session changes or the user returns to the application.
10. Handle expired sessions and revoked permissions safely.

## 7. SECURE ROLE MANAGEMENT

Use the existing `user_roles` table.

Requirements:

- Students receive only the Student role through the trusted registration process.
- Registration requests must never grant Coordinator or Admin permissions.
- Do not use editable profile fields or user-controlled metadata as the source of authorization.
- Do not expose a service-role key to the browser.
- Privileged role assignment must use a trusted administrative process.
- Prevent users from modifying their own role assignments.
- Ensure that role checks cannot be bypassed by changing browser state, local storage, or frontend requests.

If the existing Phase 0 database schema does not enforce these rules, create a safe, version-controlled migration to correct the issue without destroying existing data.

- `/`

### Staff routes

- `/pending-approval`
- `/account-status`

Security requirements:

4. Rejected students must not access either dashboard.

6. Invalid or missing role data must fail closed.
7. Never rely on hiding sidebar items as the only access control.
8. Enforce permissions at the database and server boundaries using RLS and trusted backend operations.
9. Recheck authorization when the session changes or the user returns to the application.
10. Handle expired sessions and revoked permissions safely.

Use the existing `user_roles` table.

Requirements:

PHASE 2 — INTERNSHIP SHARING

Build on top of Phases 0 and 1. Do NOT modify or break existing auth, roles, approval flow, or dashboard shells. Only add the following and fill the existing empty "Internships" pages.

A) STAFF SIDE (Coordinator and Admin, same page) — sidebar tab "Internships"
1. Table of all internships: title, company, type, domain, last date, number of interested/applied students, actions (View, Edit, Delete). Search box and filter by type and domain.
2. "Add Internship" button opens a form with these fields:
   - Apply Link (paste the external link, e.g. from Unstop/Internshala) — required, must be a valid URL
   - Title (required), Company (required)
   - Type: Internship | Training | International
   - Domain (e.g. Web Development, Data Science, AI/ML, IoT, Other)
   - Duration, Stipend (text, e.g. "Unpaid" or "10000/month")
   - Location Mode: Remote | Onsite | Hybrid
   - Last Date (date picker)
   - Description (multiline)
3. On Publish: save the internship, show a success toast, and create one notification for every approved student: "New internship: <title> at <company>" linking to that internship.
4. Edit and Delete (with a confirmation dialog). Deleting an internship also removes related student_internships rows.
5. Internship detail page for staff (/staff/internships/:id): shows all details, and a table of students who set a status on it (name, PRN, branch, year, status, last updated), with a filter by status and a count summary per status.

B) STUDENT SIDE — sidebar tab "Internships"
1. Card grid of all internships, newest first. Each card shows: title, company, type badge (International badge highlighted), domain, duration, stipend, location mode, last date with a "X days left" or "Expired" label.
2. Search box and filters: type, domain, location mode. Option to hide expired internships.
3. Clicking a card opens a detail page (/student/internships/:id) with the full description and an "Apply" button that opens the apply link in a new tab (rel="noopener noreferrer").
4. "My Status" selector on the card and the detail page: Interested | Applied | Selected | Ongoing | Completed. Saving creates or updates the student's row in student_internships (unique per student and internship). Show the current status as a badge on the card.
   - When status becomes "Ongoing" and start_date is empty, ask the student for a start date.
   - When status becomes "Completed", ask for an end date.
5. Student Home: add a section "New Internships" showing the latest 3.

C) NOTIFICATIONS
1. Make the top-bar bell show an unread count for the logged-in user.
2. Notifications page lists items newest first; clicking marks it read and opens its link.

D) SECURITY (RLS)
- All approved users can read internships.
- Only staff can insert, update, delete internships.
- A student can insert/update/read only their own student_internships rows. Staff can read all of them.
- Notifications: a user can read and mark read only their own.

ACCEPTANCE CHECKLIST — report each item as PASS or FAIL and fix any FAIL
[ ] Staff can add an internship with a pasted link and all fields; invalid URL is rejected
[ ] After publishing, an approved student sees the new card in the Internships tab
[ ] After publishing, the student gets a notification and the bell shows the count
[ ] Student can open details, the Apply button opens the link in a new tab
[ ] Student can set each of the 5 statuses; status persists after refresh
[ ] Staff internship detail page shows which students set which status
[ ] Staff can edit and delete an internship; a student cannot access these actions
[ ] A student cannot see another student's status (verify RLS)
[ ] Filters and search work on both staff and student pages
[ ] Everything works properly on a mobile screen

:::writing{variant="document" id="58321"}
# PHASE 0 — PROJECT SETUP + DATABASE
## Internship Performance Tracking System

You are a senior full-stack developer and software architect. Build Phase 0 of a production-ready web application called **Internship Performance Tracking System (IPTS)**.

The application will help a college manage internship opportunities, student progress, weekly reports, staff coordination, and international training opportunities through a centralized platform.

Follow the instructions carefully. Work only on Phase 0. Do not start implementing future phases.

## 1. First, Inspect the Project

Before making changes:

1. Inspect the existing project files and folder structure.
2. Identify the current framework, dependencies, database configuration, and environment variables.
3. If an existing project is present, preserve its working functionality and reuse the existing technology stack wherever practical.
4. If the project is empty, initialize it using React, Vite, TypeScript, and Supabase.
5. Do not delete existing files or replace the entire project without a clear technical reason.
6. Create a brief implementation plan and then proceed with the setup.

## 2. Technology Stack

Use the following stack for a new project:

- Frontend: React.js + Vite + TypeScript
- Styling: Tailwind CSS
- UI Components: shadcn/ui where appropriate
- Backend and Database: Supabase
- Database: PostgreSQL
- Form Validation: Zod
- Icons: Lucide React
- Version Control: Git

Use stable, mutually compatible package versions.

If the existing project already uses an equivalent working stack, do not unnecessarily migrate it.

## 3. Project Structure

Organize the application into a maintainable structure similar to:

src/
  components/
  pages/
  layouts/
  hooks/
  lib/
    supabase.ts
  services/
  types/
  utils/
  App.tsx
  main.tsx

supabase/
  migrations/

public/

Create additional folders only when they are useful. Keep database access, UI components, types, and application logic separated.

## 4. Supabase Configuration

Configure Supabase using environment variables.

Create a `.env.example` file containing placeholders such as:

VITE_SUPABASE_URL=
VITE_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY=

Use the current Supabase client conventions and the publishable key intended for browser use.

Important security requirements:

- Never expose a Supabase secret key or service-role key in frontend code.
- Never commit real credentials to Git.
- Do not hardcode passwords, API keys, or private tokens.
- Validate required environment variables and show a useful configuration error if they are missing.
- Document how to create a Supabase project and configure its URL and publishable key.
- Do not assume that the database is connected until the connection has actually been tested.

## 5. Create the Initial Database Schema

Create version-controlled SQL migration files inside `supabase/migrations/`.

Create the following tables with appropriate PostgreSQL data types, primary keys, foreign keys, constraints, and timestamps.

### A. profiles

Purpose: Store student and staff profile information.

Fields:

- id: UUID primary key referencing auth.users(id), with appropriate deletion behavior
- full_name: text
- student_id: text, nullable for staff
- department: text
- academic_year: text
- email: text
- avatar_url: text, nullable
- bio: text, nullable
- skills: text array or suitable structured representation
- approval_status: pending, approved, or rejected
- created_at: timestamptz
- updated_at: timestamptz

Requirements:

- A profile belongs to an authenticated Supabase user.
- Email and profile information must be validated.
- Enforce appropriate uniqueness for student IDs when present.
- Do not store passwords in this table.
- The initial approval status for new student registrations must be pending.
- Use appropriate defaults without allowing users to choose privileged roles.

### B. user_roles

Purpose: Store application roles separately from editable profile information.

Fields:

- id: UUID primary key
- user_id: UUID referencing auth.users(id)
- role: student, coordinator, or admin
- created_at: timestamptz

Requirements:

- Prevent duplicate assignments of the same role to the same user.
- Use database constraints where appropriate.
- Never allow a public signup request to assign itself the coordinator or admin role.
- Do not trust role values supplied by the frontend.
- Privileged role assignment must be performed through a trusted administrative process.

### C. internships

Purpose: Store opportunities published by authorized staff.

Fields:

- id: UUID primary key
- title: text
- company_name: text
- opportunity_url: text
- internship_type: text
- domain: text
- duration: text, nullable
- stipend: text, nullable
- application_deadline: timestamptz, nullable
- description: text
- eligibility: text, nullable
- status: draft, published, expired, or archived
- created_by: UUID referencing the creator's profile or authenticated user
- published_at: timestamptz, nullable
- created_at: timestamptz
- updated_at: timestamptz

Requirements:

- Validate URLs and required fields at the application layer.
- Only authorized staff should be able to create or modify opportunities.
- Students must not be able to publish, edit, or delete opportunities.
- Published opportunities should be readable by approved students.
- Keep status values consistent.

### D. student_internships

Purpose: Track the relationship between students and opportunities.

Fields:

- id: UUID primary key
- student_id: UUID referencing profiles(id)
- internship_id: UUID referencing internships(id)
- application_status: interested, applied, selected, ongoing, completed, or rejected
- applied_at: timestamptz, nullable
- created_at: timestamptz
- updated_at: timestamptz

Requirements:

- Prevent duplicate tracking records for the same student and internship.
- Students may update only their own application records.
- Staff may view application statuses according to their permissions.
- A student must not be able to mark an internship as completed without any further verification if the application requires staff review.

### E. weekly_reports

Purpose: Prepare for the weekly internship progress reporting feature in a future phase.

Fields:

- id: UUID primary key
- student_internship_id: UUID referencing student_internships(id)
- week_number: integer
- learning_summary: text
- tools_used: text or structured representation
- completed_tasks: text
- challenges: text, nullable
- next_week_plan: text, nullable
- hours_spent: numeric
- proof_url: text, nullable
- review_status: pending, approved, or needs_improvement
- reviewer_comment: text, nullable
- reviewed_by: UUID, nullable
- reviewed_at: timestamptz, nullable
- created_at: timestamptz
- updated_at: timestamptz

Requirements:

- Enforce a positive week number.
- Validate hours and text inputs.
- Prevent duplicate reports for the same internship and week where appropriate.
- Only authorized staff may approve or request improvements.
- Students may access only their own reports.

### F. announcements

Purpose: Prepare for staff announcements in a future phase.

Fields:

- id: UUID primary key
- title: text
- content: text
- created_by: UUID
- published_at: timestamptz, nullable
- created_at: timestamptz
- updated_at: timestamptz

Only authorized staff should be able to create, modify, and delete announcements.

### G. notifications

Purpose: Prepare for notifications in future phases.

Fields:

- id: UUID primary key
- user_id: UUID referencing auth.users(id)
- title: text
- message: text
- notification_type: text
- related_entity_id: UUID, nullable
- is_read: boolean default false
- created_at: timestamptz

Users must only be able to read and update their own notifications. Notification creation must be restricted to trusted server-side or database processes.

### H. documents

Purpose: Prepare for offer letters, certificates, and other internship documents.

Fields:

- id: UUID primary key
- user_id: UUID referencing auth.users(id)
- student_internship_id: UUID, nullable
- document_type: text
- file_name: text
- storage_path: text
- created_at: timestamptz

Requirements:

- Store file metadata in PostgreSQL and files in private Supabase Storage buckets.
- Do not store uploaded file contents directly in database rows.
- Document access must be restricted to the owner and explicitly authorized staff.
- Do not create a public bucket for confidential student documents.

### I. community_messages

Purpose: Prepare the database for a future community chat.

Fields:

- id: UUID primary key
- sender_id: UUID referencing auth.users(id)
- message: text
- created_at: timestamptz
- updated_at: timestamptz, nullable

Add a suitable foundation for future message moderation. Do not implement the chat interface in Phase 0.

## 6. Database Security and Row Level Security

Enable Row Level Security (RLS) on all tables.

Create appropriate policies based on the user's authenticated identity and trusted role assignments.

Required security principles:

1. Students can access only their own private profile fields and personal progress records, except for information explicitly intended to be public within the approved community.
2. Students cannot approve their own registration.
3. Students cannot assign themselves privileged roles.
4. Only authorized coordinators and admins can manage internships and review student reports.
5. Only admins can manage coordinator assignments.
6. Students cannot read other students' confidential documents or private reports.
7. Only staff can manage announcements.
8. Users can access only their own notifications.
9. Chat access must be restricted to eligible community members when implemented.
10. Never implement security using frontend checks alone.

Use safe SQL functions and avoid recursive RLS policies. If a privileged role-checking function is needed, implement it with carefully restricted execution permissions and a safe search path.

Do not expose private role information through an unrestricted public endpoint.

## 7. Profile Creation Preparation

Prepare a secure database-side mechanism for creating a profile when a new user is registered.

Requirements:

- Profile creation must use the authenticated user's UUID.
- A new student must default to pending approval.
- Role assignment must not trust user-provided metadata.
- Public signup must never grant admin or coordinator permissions.
- The setup must fail safely if a profile cannot be created.
- Ensure database triggers cannot be abused to escalate privileges.

Do not build the full login, signup, or approval interface in Phase 0. That belongs to Phase 1.

## 8. Initial Frontend

Create a clean, responsive application shell with:

- Application name: Internship Performance Tracking System
- Short description: Manage internship opportunities and student progress in one place.
- A basic landing page.
- A simple setup/status page showing whether required environment configuration is present.
- A clean loading state and a useful error state.
- A responsive layout suitable for desktop and mobile.

Do not implement the real Student Dashboard, Staff Dashboard, internship management screens, weekly reports, chat, resume builder, or analytics yet.

Do not display fabricated student counts or fake progress statistics.

## 9. Database Migrations and Reproducibility

Create SQL migrations that can be applied to a fresh Supabase project.

Requirements:

- Keep migrations version-controlled.
- Use foreign keys and indexes where needed.
- Add indexes for common queries such as student IDs, opportunity status, deadlines, student applications, and report review status.
- Use appropriate check constraints for statuses and numeric values.
- Ensure the migration sequence works on a clean database.
- Avoid destructive changes to an existing database.
- Do not create unnecessary duplicate tables or incompatible column definitions.
- Use consistent naming conventions.

Do not insert fake student accounts or real-looking sample records into production tables.

:::writing{variant="document" id="58321"}
# PHASE 0 — PROJECT SETUP + DATABASE
## Internship Performance Tracking System

You are a senior full-stack developer and software architect. Build Phase 0 of a production-ready web application called **Internship Performance Tracking System (IPTS)**.

The application will help a college manage internship opportunities, student progress, weekly reports, staff coordination, and international training opportunities through a centralized platform.

Follow the instructions carefully. Work only on Phase 0. Do not start implementing future phases.

## 1. First, Inspect the Project

Before making changes:

1. Inspect the existing project files and folder structure.
2. Identify the current framework, dependencies, database configuration, and environment variables.
3. If an existing project is present, preserve its working functionality and reuse the existing technology stack wherever practical.
4. If the project is empty, initialize it using React, Vite, TypeScript, and Supabase.
5. Do not delete existing files or replace the entire project without a clear technical reason.
6. Create a brief implementation plan and then proceed with the setup.

## 2. Technology Stack

Use the following stack for a new project:

- Frontend: React.js + Vite + TypeScript
- Styling: Tailwind CSS
- UI Components: shadcn/ui where appropriate
- Backend and Database: Supabase
- Database: PostgreSQL
- Form Validation: Zod
- Icons: Lucide React
- Version Control: Git

Use stable, mutually compatible package versions.

If the existing project already uses an equivalent working stack, do not unnecessarily migrate it.

## 3. Project Structure

Organize the application into a maintainable structure similar to:

src/
  components/
  pages/
  layouts/
  hooks/
  lib/
    supabase.ts
  services/
  types/
  utils/
  App.tsx
  main.tsx

supabase/
  migrations/

public/

Create additional folders only when they are useful. Keep database access, UI components, types, and application logic separated.

## 4. Supabase Configuration

Configure Supabase using environment variables.

Create a `.env.example` file containing placeholders such as:

VITE_SUPABASE_URL=
VITE_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY=

Use the current Supabase client conventions and the publishable key intended for browser use.

Important security requirements:

- Never expose a Supabase secret key or service-role key in frontend code.
- Never commit real credentials to Git.
- Do not hardcode passwords, API keys, or private tokens.
- Validate required environment variables and show a useful configuration error if they are missing.
- Document how to create a Supabase project and configure its URL and publishable key.
- Do not assume that the database is connected until the connection has actually been tested.

## 5. Create the Initial Database Schema

Create version-controlled SQL migration files inside `supabase/migrations/`.

Create the following tables with appropriate PostgreSQL data types, primary keys, foreign keys, constraints, and timestamps.

### A. profiles

Purpose: Store student and staff profile information.

Fields:

- id: UUID primary key referencing auth.users(id), with appropriate deletion behavior
- full_name: text
- student_id: text, nullable for staff
- department: text
- academic_year: text
- email: text
- avatar_url: text, nullable
- bio: text, nullable
- skills: text array or suitable structured representation
- approval_status: pending, approved, or rejected
- created_at: timestamptz
- updated_at: timestamptz

Requirements:

- A profile belongs to an authenticated Supabase user.
- Email and profile information must be validated.
- Enforce appropriate uniqueness for student IDs when present.
- Do not store passwords in this table.
- The initial approval status for new student registrations must be pending.
- Use appropriate defaults without allowing users to choose privileged roles.

### B. user_roles

Purpose: Store application roles separately from editable profile information.

Fields:

- id: UUID primary key
- user_id: UUID referencing auth.users(id)
- role: student, coordinator, or admin
- created_at: timestamptz

Requirements:

- Prevent duplicate assignments of the same role to the same user.
- Use database constraints where appropriate.
- Never allow a public signup request to assign itself the coordinator or admin role.
- Do not trust role values supplied by the frontend.
- Privileged role assignment must be performed through a trusted administrative process.

### C. internships

Purpose: Store opportunities published by authorized staff.

Fields:

- id: UUID primary key
- title: text
- company_name: text
- opportunity_url: text
- internship_type: text
- domain: text
- duration: text, nullable
- stipend: text, nullable
- application_deadline: timestamptz, nullable
- description: text
- eligibility: text, nullable
- status: draft, published, expired, or archived
- created_by: UUID referencing the creator's profile or authenticated user
- published_at: timestamptz, nullable
- created_at: timestamptz
- updated_at: timestamptz

Requirements:

- Validate URLs and required fields at the application layer.
- Only authorized staff should be able to create or modify opportunities.
- Students must not be able to publish, edit, or delete opportunities.
- Published opportunities should be readable by approved students.
- Keep status values consistent.

### D. student_internships

Purpose: Track the relationship between students and opportunities.

Fields:

- id: UUID primary key
- student_id: UUID referencing profiles(id)
- internship_id: UUID referencing internships(id)
- application_status: interested, applied, selected, ongoing, completed, or rejected
- applied_at: timestamptz, nullable
- created_at: timestamptz
- updated_at: timestamptz

Requirements:

- Prevent duplicate tracking records for the same student and internship.
- Students may update only their own application records.
- Staff may view application statuses according to their permissions.
- A student must not be able to mark an internship as completed without any further verification if the application requires staff review.

### E. weekly_reports

Purpose: Prepare for the weekly internship progress reporting feature in a future phase.

Fields:

- id: UUID primary key
- student_internship_id: UUID referencing student_internships(id)
- week_number: integer
- learning_summary: text
- tools_used: text or structured representation
- completed_tasks: text
- challenges: text, nullable
- next_week_plan: text, nullable
- hours_spent: numeric
- proof_url: text, nullable
- review_status: pending, approved, or needs_improvement
- reviewer_comment: text, nullable
- reviewed_by: UUID, nullable
- reviewed_at: timestamptz, nullable
- created_at: timestamptz
- updated_at: timestamptz

Requirements:

- Enforce a positive week number.
- Validate hours and text inputs.
- Prevent duplicate reports for the same internship and week where appropriate.
- Only authorized staff may approve or request improvements.
- Students may access only their own reports.

### F. announcements

Purpose: Prepare for staff announcements in a future phase.

Fields:

- id: UUID primary key
- title: text
- content: text
- created_by: UUID
- published_at: timestamptz, nullable
- created_at: timestamptz
- updated_at: timestamptz

Only authorized staff should be able to create, modify, and delete announcements.

### G. notifications

Purpose: Prepare for notifications in future phases.

Fields:

- id: UUID primary key
- user_id: UUID referencing auth.users(id)
- title: text
- message: text
- notification_type: text
- related_entity_id: UUID, nullable
- is_read: boolean default false
- created_at: timestamptz

Users must only be able to read and update their own notifications. Notification creation must be restricted to trusted server-side or database processes.

### H. documents

Purpose: Prepare for offer letters, certificates, and other internship documents.

Fields:

- id: UUID primary key
- user_id: UUID referencing auth.users(id)
- student_internship_id: UUID, nullable
- document_type: text
- file_name: text
- storage_path: text
- created_at: timestamptz

Requirements:

- Store file metadata in PostgreSQL and files in private Supabase Storage buckets.
- Do not store uploaded file contents directly in database rows.
- Document access must be restricted to the owner and explicitly authorized staff.
- Do not create a public bucket for confidential student documents.

### I. community_messages

Purpose: Prepare the database for a future community chat.

Fields:

- id: UUID primary key
- sender_id: UUID referencing auth.users(id)
- message: text
- created_at: timestamptz
- updated_at: timestamptz, nullable

Add a suitable foundation for future message moderation. Do not implement the chat interface in Phase 0.

## 6. Database Security and Row Level Security

Enable Row Level Security (RLS) on all tables.

Create appropriate policies based on the user's authenticated identity and trusted role assignments.

Required security principles:

1. Students can access only their own private profile fields and personal progress records, except for information explicitly intended to be public within the approved community.
2. Students cannot approve their own registration.
3. Students cannot assign themselves privileged roles.
4. Only authorized coordinators and admins can manage internships and review student reports.
5. Only admins can manage coordinator assignments.
6. Students cannot read other students' confidential documents or private reports.
7. Only staff can manage announcements.
8. Users can access only their own notifications.
9. Chat access must be restricted to eligible community members when implemented.
10. Never implement security using frontend checks alone.

Use safe SQL functions and avoid recursive RLS policies. If a privileged role-checking function is needed, implement it with carefully restricted execution permissions and a safe search path.

Do not expose private role information through an unrestricted public endpoint.

## 7. Profile Creation Preparation

Prepare a secure database-side mechanism for creating a profile when a new user is registered.

Requirements:

- Profile creation must use the authenticated user's UUID.
- A new student must default to pending approval.
- Role assignment must not trust user-provided metadata.
- Public signup must never grant admin or coordinator permissions.
- The setup must fail safely if a profile cannot be created.
- Ensure database triggers cannot be abused to escalate privileges.

Do not build the full login, signup, or approval interface in Phase 0. That belongs to Phase 1.

## 8. Initial Frontend

Create a clean, responsive application shell with:

- Application name: Internship Performance Tracking System
- Short description: Manage internship opportunities and student progress in one place.
- A basic landing page.
- A simple setup/status page showing whether required environment configuration is present.
- A clean loading state and a useful error state.
- A responsive layout suitable for desktop and mobile.

Do not implement the real Student Dashboard, Staff Dashboard, internship management screens, weekly reports, chat, resume builder, or analytics yet.

Do not display fabricated student counts or fake progress statistics.

## 9. Database Migrations and Reproducibility

Create SQL migrations that can be applied to a fresh Supabase project.

- Use foreign keys and indexes where needed.

- Use appropriate check constraints for statuses and numeric values.
- Ensure the migration sequence works on a clean database.
- Avoid destructive changes to an existing database.
- Do not create unnecessary duplicate tables or incompatible column definitions.
- Use consistent naming conventions.

Do not insert fake student accounts or real-looking sample records into production tables.

4. Only authorized coordinators and admins can manage internships and review student reports.
5. Only admins can manage coordinator assignments.
6. Students cannot read other students' confidential documents or private reports.
7. Only staff can manage announcements.
8. Users can access only their own notifications.
9. Chat access must be restricted to eligible community members when implemented.
10. Never implement security using frontend checks alone.

Use safe SQL functions and avoid recursive RLS policies. If a privileged role-checking function is needed, implement it with carefully restricted execution permissions and a safe search path.

Do not expose private role information through an unrestricted public endpoint.

## 7. Profile Creation Preparation

Prepare a secure database-side mechanism for creating a profile when a new user is registered.

Requirements:

- Profile creation must use the authenticated user's UUID.
- A new student must default to pending approval.
- Role assignment must not trust user-provided metadata.
- Public signup must never grant admin or coordinator permissions.
- The setup must fail safely if a profile cannot be created.
- Ensure database triggers cannot be abused to escalate privileges.

Do not build the full login, signup, or approval interface in Phase 0. That belongs to Phase 1.

## 8. Initial Frontend

Create a clean, responsive application shell with:

- Application name: Internship Performance Tracking System
- Short description: Manage internship opportunities and student progress in one place.
- A basic landing page.
- A simple setup/status page showing whether required environment configuration is present.
- A clean loading state and a useful error state.
- A responsive layout suitable for desktop and mobile.

Do not implement the real Student Dashboard, Staff Dashboard, internship management screens, weekly reports, chat, resume builder, or analytics yet.

Do not display fabricated student counts or fake progress statistics.

## 9. Database Migrations and Reproducibility

Create SQL migrations that can be applied to a fresh Supabase project.

Requirements:

- Keep migrations version-controlled.
- Use foreign keys and indexes where needed.
- Add indexes for common queries such as student IDs, opportunity status, deadlines, student applications, and report review status.
- Use appropriate check constraints for statuses and numeric values.
- Ensure the migration sequence works on a clean database.
- Avoid destructive changes to an existing database.
- Do not create unnecessary duplicate tables or incompatible column definitions.
- Use consistent naming conventions.

Do not insert fake student accounts or real-looking sample records into production tables.

## 10. Documentation

Create a `README.md` that explains:

1. Project purpose.
2. Technology stack.

- Install dependencies if required.
- Run TypeScript checks.
- Run the production build.
- Run available linting and tests.
- Inspect migration SQL for syntax and policy issues.
- Verify that environment configuration errors are handled cleanly.
- Test the database connection only if valid Supabase credentials are available.
- Do not claim that database migrations or security policies have been tested against a live database unless they actually have been executed.
- Fix any errors introduced by your changes.

If live Supabase credentials are unavailable, clearly document which database checks remain to be performed.

## 12. Scope Restrictions

This is Phase 0 only.

Do not implement:

- Full authentication screens.
- Role-based dashboard routing.
- Registration approval workflows.
- Internship publishing UI.
- Weekly report submission or review UI.
- Real-time chat.
- Resume generation.
- Excel/PDF export.
- Inactive student monitoring.
- Leaderboards or streaks.

These features will be implemented in later phases after the current phase has been verified.

<WritingBlock id="58321" variant="document"># PHASE 0 — PROJECT SETUP + DATABASE
## Internship Performance Tracking System

You are a senior full-stack developer and software architect. Build Phase 0 of a production-ready web application called **Internship Performance Tracking System (IPTS)**.

The application will help a college manage internship opportunities, student progress, weekly reports, staff coordination, and international training opportunities through a centralized platform.

Follow the instructions carefully. Work only on Phase 0. Do not start implementing future phases.

## 1. First, Inspect the Project

Before making changes:

1. Inspect the existing project files and folder structure.
2. Identify the current framework, dependencies, database configuration, and environment variables.
3. If an existing project is present, preserve its working functionality and reuse the existing technology stack wherever practical.
4. If the project is empty, initialize it using React, Vite, TypeScript, and Supabase.
5. Do not delete existing files or replace the entire project without a clear technical reason.
6. Create a brief implementation plan and then proceed with the setup.

## 2. Technology Stack

Use the following stack for a new project:

- Frontend: React.js + Vite + TypeScript
- Styling: Tailwind CSS
- UI Components: shadcn/ui where appropriate
- Backend and Database: Supabase
- Database: PostgreSQL
- Form Validation: Zod
- Icons: Lucide React
- Version Control: Git

Use stable, mutually compatible package versions.

If the existing project already uses an equivalent working stack, do not unnecessarily migrate it.

## 3. Project Structure

Organize the application into a maintainable structure similar to:

src/
  components/
  pages/
  layouts/
  hooks/
  lib/
    supabase.ts
  services/
  types/
  utils/
  App.tsx
  main.tsx

supabase/
  migrations/

public/

Create additional folders only when they are useful. Keep database access, UI components, types, and application logic separated.

## 4. Supabase Configuration

Configure Supabase using environment variables.

Create a `.env.example` file containing placeholders such as:

VITE_SUPABASE_URL=
VITE_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY=

Use the current Supabase client conventions and the publishable key intended for browser use.

Important security requirements:

- Never expose a Supabase secret key or service-role key in frontend code.
- Never commit real credentials to Git.
- Do not hardcode passwords, API keys, or private tokens.
- Validate required environment variables and show a useful configuration error if they are missing.
- Document how to create a Supabase project and configure its URL and publishable key.
- Do not assume that the database is connected until the connection has actually been tested.

## 5. Create the Initial Database Schema

Create version-controlled SQL migration files inside `supabase/migrations/`.

Create the following tables with appropriate PostgreSQL data types, primary keys, foreign keys, constraints, and timestamps.

### A. profiles

Purpose: Store student and staff profile information.

Fields:

- id: UUID primary key referencing auth.users(id), with appropriate deletion behavior
- full_name: text
- student_id: text, nullable for staff
- department: text
- academic_year: text
- email: text
- avatar_url: text, nullable
- bio: text, nullable
- skills: text array or suitable structured representation
- approval_status: pending, approved, or rejected
- created_at: timestamptz
- updated_at: timestamptz

Requirements:

- A profile belongs to an authenticated Supabase user.
- Email and profile information must be validated.
- Enforce appropriate uniqueness for student IDs when present.
- Do not store passwords in this table.
- The initial approval status for new student registrations must be pending.
- Use appropriate defaults without allowing users to choose privileged roles.

### B. user_roles

Purpose: Store application roles separately from editable profile information.

Fields:

- id: UUID primary key
- user_id: UUID referencing auth.users(id)
- role: student, coordinator, or admin
- created_at: timestamptz

Requirements:

- Prevent duplicate assignments of the same role to the same user.
- Use database constraints where appropriate.
- Never allow a public signup request to assign itself the coordinator or admin role.
- Do not trust role values supplied by the frontend.
- Privileged role assignment must be performed through a trusted administrative process.

### C. internships

Purpose: Store opportunities published by authorized staff.

Fields:

- id: UUID primary key
- title: text
- company_name: text
- opportunity_url: text
- internship_type: text
- domain: text
- duration: text, nullable
- stipend: text, nullable
- application_deadline: timestamptz, nullable
- description: text
- eligibility: text, nullable
- status: draft, published, expired, or archived
- created_by: UUID referencing the creator's profile or authenticated user
- published_at: timestamptz, nullable
- created_at: timestamptz
- updated_at: timestamptz

Requirements:

- Validate URLs and required fields at the application layer.
- Only authorized staff should be able to create or modify opportunities.
- Students must not be able to publish, edit, or delete opportunities.
- Published opportunities should be readable by approved students.
- Keep status values consistent.

### D. student_internships

Purpose: Track the relationship between students and opportunities.

Fields:

- id: UUID primary key
- student_id: UUID referencing profiles(id)
- internship_id: UUID referencing internships(id)
- application_status: interested, applied, selected, ongoing, completed, or rejected
- applied_at: timestamptz, nullable
- created_at: timestamptz
- updated_at: timestamptz

Requirements:

- Prevent duplicate tracking records for the same student and internship.
- Students may update only their own application records.
- Staff may view application statuses according to their permissions.
- A student must not be able to mark an internship as completed without any further verification if the application requires staff review.

### E. weekly_reports

Purpose: Prepare for the weekly internship progress reporting feature in a future phase.

Fields:

- id: UUID primary key
- student_internship_id: UUID referencing student_internships(id)
- week_number: integer
- learning_summary: text
- tools_used: text or structured representation
- completed_tasks: text
- challenges: text, nullable
- next_week_plan: text, nullable
- hours_spent: numeric
- proof_url: text, nullable
- review_status: pending, approved, or needs_improvement
- reviewer_comment: text, nullable
- reviewed_by: UUID, nullable
- reviewed_at: timestamptz, nullable
- created_at: timestamptz
- updated_at: timestamptz

Requirements:

- Enforce a positive week number.
- Validate hours and text inputs.
- Prevent duplicate reports for the same internship and week where appropriate.
- Only authorized staff may approve or request improvements.
- Students may access only their own reports.

### F. announcements

Purpose: Prepare for staff announcements in a future phase.

Fields:

- id: UUID primary key
- title: text
- content: text
- created_by: UUID
- published_at: timestamptz, nullable
- created_at: timestamptz
- updated_at: timestamptz

Only authorized staff should be able to create, modify, and delete announcements.

### G. notifications

Purpose: Prepare for notifications in future phases.

Fields:

- id: UUID primary key
- user_id: UUID referencing auth.users(id)
- title: text
- message: text
- notification_type: text
- related_entity_id: UUID, nullable
- is_read: boolean default false
- created_at: timestamptz

Users must only be able to read and update their own notifications. Notification creation must be restricted to trusted server-side or database processes.

### H. documents

Purpose: Prepare for offer letters, certificates, and other internship documents.

Fields:

- id: UUID primary key
- user_id: UUID referencing auth.users(id)
- student_internship_id: UUID, nullable
- document_type: text
- file_name: text
- storage_path: text
- created_at: timestamptz

Requirements:

- Store file metadata in PostgreSQL and files in private Supabase Storage buckets.
- Do not store uploaded file contents directly in database rows.
- Document access must be restricted to the owner and explicitly authorized staff.
- Do not create a public bucket for confidential student documents.

### I. community_messages

Purpose: Prepare the database for a future community chat.

Fields:

- id: UUID primary key
- sender_id: UUID referencing auth.users(id)
- message: text
- created_at: timestamptz
- updated_at: timestamptz, nullable

Add a suitable foundation for future message moderation. Do not implement the chat interface in Phase 0.

# Internship Performance Tracking System: संपूर्ण प्लॅन

## 1. उद्देश

| मुद्दा       | तपशील                                                                  |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| समस्या       | Excel भरा, Google Form भरा, प्रत्येक विद्यार्थ्याचं manually बघा       |
| उपाय         | एकच वेब ॲप: internships शेअर करणे, progress track करणे, community chat |
| शेवटचं ध्येय | कॉलेजमध्ये International Training Opportunities चं culture तयार करणे   |

## 2. वापरकर्ते (Roles)

| Role        | कोण                      | Dashboard             | मुख्य अधिकार                                             |
| ----------- | ------------------------ | --------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| Student     | नोंदणी केलेले विद्यार्थी | Student Dashboard     | स्वतःचा progress टाकणे, internships बघणे, chat           |
| Coordinator | तुम्ही                   | Staff Dashboard       | Internship शेअर करणे, progress बघणे, review, chat manage |
| Admin       | Admin व्यक्ती            | Staff Dashboard (तोच) | Coordinator सारखे सगळे अधिकार + Coordinator add/remove   |

## 3. मुख्य Flow: Internship शेअर करणे

| Step | कोण               | काय होतं                                                                                              |
| ---- | ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1    | Coordinator/Admin | Unstop वगैरे साईटवर internship बघतो, link copy करतो                                                   |
| 2    | Coordinator/Admin | ॲपमध्ये "Add Internship" उघडून link paste करतो                                                        |
| 3    | Coordinator/Admin | Title, Company, Type, Domain, Duration, Stipend, Last Date, Description manually भरतो                 |
| 4    | System            | Publish होताच सर्व approved students ना card दिसतं आणि notification जातं                              |
| 5    | Student           | Details वाचतो, Apply link उघडतो, स्वतःचा status ठेवतो (Interested/Applied/Selected/Ongoing/Completed) |
| 6    | Coordinator/Admin | कोणत्या student ने काय status ठेवला ते internship च्या पानावर बघतो                                    |

## 4. Progress Flow

| Step | कोण         | काय होतं                                                                                                                       |
| ---- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| 1    | Student     | Internship "Ongoing" झाल्यावर दर आठवड्याला report भरतो                                                                         |
| 2    | Student     | Report मध्ये: Week no., काय शिकलो, कोणती tools वापरली, कोणती कामं पूर्ण केली, अडचणी, पुढच्या आठवड्याचा plan, hours, proof link |
| 3    | Coordinator | Pending reports बघतो, Approve किंवा Needs Improvement + comment देतो                                                           |
| 4    | System      | Student ला notification, आणि progress % आपोआप वाढतो                                                                            |
| 5    | Coordinator | 14 दिवस report नसलेले students "Inactive" list मध्ये बघतो                                                                      |

## 5. Student Dashboard: पानं

| पान            | काय असतं                                                              |
| -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Home           | Progress %, चालू internship, Announcements, नवीन internships          |

| Weekly Reports | नवीन report, जुने reports, feedback                                   |
| Community      | #announcements (फक्त वाचणे), #community (chat)                        |
| Resume         | Profile वरून PDF resume                                               |
| Notifications  | सगळ्या सूचना                                                          |

## 6. Staff Dashboard: पानं

| पान               | काय असतं                                                    |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| Overview          | एकूण students, active interns, pending reports, charts      |
| Internships       | Add / Edit / Delete, कोणत्या student ने काय status ठेवला    |
| Students          | List, search/filter, एका student चा पूर्ण progress          |
| Report Reviews    | Pending reports, Approve/Needs Improvement + comment        |
| Inactive Students | 14 दिवस report नसलेले                                       |

| Manage Staff      | फक्त Admin                                                  |

| Phase                              | काय बनतं                                                 | पूर्ण झाल्याची खूण (तपासणी)                                                    |
| ---------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **0** Setup + Database             | Project आणि tables                                       | ॲप चालतं, Signup केला की profile तयार होतो                                     |
| **1** Login + Roles + Approval     | 3 roles, 2 dashboards, approval                          | Student approve होईपर्यंत आत जाऊ शकत नाही; Student /staff उघडू शकत नाही        |
| **2** Internship Sharing           | Staff ने टाकलेली internship student ला दिसते             | Staff ने Publish केलं, student ला card दिसलं, status ठेवता आला, staff ला दिसला |
| **3** Weekly Reports + Review      | Report भरणे, review                                      | Student ने भरलं, Staff ने approve केलं, student ला feedback दिसला              |
| **4** Community                    | Chat, Announcements, Notifications                       | दोन accounts मध्ये chat realtime दिसतं                                         |
| **5** Documents + Profile + Resume | Upload, profile, PDF                                     | Offer Letter upload झालं, Resume PDF बनला                                      |
| **6** Overview + Export + Inactive | Charts, Excel, inactive list                             | Excel download होतो, inactive students दिसतात                                  |
| **7** नवीन features (नंतर)         | International Opportunities section, Leaderboard, Streak | आधीचं काही बिघडलं नाही                                                         |

## 10. प्रत्येक Phase साठी तुमची कार्यपद्धती

| Step | कृती                                                                              |
| ---- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1    | एका वेळी फक्त एकच Phase Antigravity ला द्या                                       |
| 2    | Phase संपल्यावर वरची "तपासणी" स्वतः करून बघा (दोन accounts: एक student, एक staff) |
| 3    | सगळं बरोबर असेल तरच पुढचा Phase                                                   |
| 4    | चूक असेल तर पुढे न जाता तीच चूक Antigravity ला सांगून सुधारून घ्या                |

## 11. माझी शिफारस

Phase 2 (Internship Sharing) आणि Phase 3 (Weekly Reports) हे ॲपचं हृदय आहेत. आधी हे दोन नीट चालवा. Chat, Resume, Leaderboard सारख्या गोष्टी नंतर कधीही जोडता येतात.

हा प्लॅन तुम्हाला मान्य असेल तर सांगा. मग Phase 0 पासून एक एक करून तयार prompts देतो.  write promt pashe -01

उदाहरणार्थ, तुम्ही `Third Year + CSE + Internship Completed` असे Filters लावले तर फक्त संबंधित विद्यार्थ्यांची यादी दिसावी.

विद्यार्थ्यांच्या रिपोर्टमध्ये पुढील माहिती असावी:

- नाव, विभाग, वर्ष आणि विद्यार्थी ID.
- किती संधी पाहिल्या आणि किती अर्ज केले.
- किती मुलाखती, निवडी आणि पूर्ण केलेल्या इंटर्नशिप आहेत.
- Certifications, Projects आणि Skills.
- शेवटचा Progress Update.
- Proof Verification Status.

यामुळे Excel प्रत्येक वेळी भरून घेण्याऐवजी तुम्ही वेबसाइटवरून आवश्यक रिपोर्ट डाउनलोड करू शकता.

# 9. Database मध्ये कोणते Tables असावेत?

सिस्टम योग्य प्रकारे बनवण्यासाठी सुरुवातीपासून डेटा स्ट्रक्चर स्पष्ट ठेवा.

| Table | काम |
|---|---|
| `profiles` | विद्यार्थ्यांचे नाव, विभाग, वर्ष, Skills आणि Profile |
| `user_roles` | Student, Coordinator आणि Admin Roles |
| `opportunities` | Internship, Training, Hackathons आणि इतर संधी |
| `applications` | कोणत्या विद्यार्थ्याने कोणत्या संधीसाठी अर्ज केला |
| `progress_updates` | विद्यार्थ्यांचे साप्ताहिक किंवा Activity Updates |
| `certifications` | Certifications आणि त्यांचे Proof |
| `projects` | Projects, GitHub Links आणि Project Status |
| `community_posts` | Posts, Announcements आणि Discussions |
| `comments` | Comments आणि Replies |
| `notifications` | नवीन संधी, Updates आणि System Alerts |
| `audit_logs` | महत्त्वाचे Admin/Coordinator Actions |

प्रत्येक Application मध्ये `student_id` आणि `opportunity_id` असावेत. त्यामुळे कोणत्या विद्यार्थ्याने कोणत्या Internship साठी अर्ज केला हे सहज कळेल.

विद्यार्थ्यांना फक्त स्वतःचे खाजगी रेकॉर्ड Edit करता यावेत. Coordinator/Admin च्या अधिकारांनुसार इतर रेकॉर्ड्स पाहणे किंवा अपडेट करणे नियंत्रित केले पाहिजे. Supabase वापरत असल्यास **Row Level Security (RLS)** आणि सुरक्षित Role Assignment आवश्यक आहेत.

# 10. विद्यार्थी Registration कसे असावे?

Registration प्रक्रिया सोपी ठेवा; पण कॉलेजच्या कम्युनिटीमध्ये अनधिकृत व्यक्ती येणार नाहीत याची काळजी घ्या.

1. विद्यार्थी नाव, ईमेल, विद्यार्थी ID, Department आणि Year देऊन Registration करेल.
2. ईमेल Verification पूर्ण करेल.
3. गरजेनुसार College ID किंवा इतर पुरावा Admin कडून तपासला जाईल.
4. मंजुरीनंतर विद्यार्थी Dashboard वापरू शकेल.
5. पहिल्या Login वेळी Skills, Interests आणि Career Goals भरेल.

**Role Security:** सार्वजनिक Registration Form मधून कोणीही स्वतःला Admin किंवा Coordinator घोषित करू शकणार नाही. हे Roles फक्त अधिकृत Admin नेच Assign करावेत.

# 11. आणखी कोणते Features जोडल्याने ही प्रणाली अधिक उपयुक्त होईल?

मी खालील गोष्टींचा प्राधान्याने विचार करेन.

- **Verified Opportunities:** संधीची अधिकृत लिंक, पडताळणी करणारी व्यक्ती आणि पडताळणीची तारीख.
- **Deadline Alerts:** अंतिम तारखेपूर्वी विद्यार्थ्यांना सूचना.
- **Skill Gap Tracking:** विद्यार्थ्याला कोणत्या Skills सुधारण्याची गरज आहे ते दाखवणे.
- **Weekly Progress:** दर आठवड्याला विद्यार्थ्यांनी केलेल्या कामाचा छोटा Update.
- **Mentorship:** Senior Students किंवा Alumni यांच्याशी संवाद.
- **Achievements Wall:** निवड, Certifications, Hackathons आणि Projects चे यश.
- **Learning Roadmaps:** AI/ML, Web Development, Cloud, Cybersecurity आणि इतर क्षेत्रांसाठी मार्गदर्शक मार्ग.
- **Placement Readiness:** Resume, GitHub, LinkedIn आणि Interview Preparation ची प्रगती.
- **Student Leaderboard:** ऐच्छिक, स्पष्ट निकषांवर आधारित आणि विद्यार्थ्यांमध्ये अस्वस्थ स्पर्धा निर्माण न करणारा.
- **Exportable Reports:** आवश्यकतेनुसार संपूर्ण कम्युनिटी किंवा विभागाचा रिपोर्ट.

विद्यार्थ्यांचे वैयक्तिक दस्तऐवज, फोन नंबर आणि खाजगी माहिती सार्वजनिक Community मध्ये दिसू नये. अधिकृत Admin आणि Coordinator यांनाच आवश्यकतेनुसार प्रवेश द्यावा.

माझ्या मते, यासाठी साधी वेबसाइट बनवण्यापेक्षा **Internship &amp; Student Progress Tracking System** नावाचे पूर्ण Web Application बनवणे योग्य राहील.

तुमच्या WhatsApp ग्रुपचा उपयोग विद्यार्थ्यांना कम्युनिटीमध्ये जोडण्यासाठी करता येईल; पण विद्यार्थ्यांची नोंदणी, त्यांचा प्रोग्रेस, संधींची माहिती, चर्चा आणि रिपोर्ट्स वेबसाइटवर ठेवता येतील.

## Internship &amp; Career Growth Hub

एकाच प्लॅटफॉर्मवर Internship + Training + Opportunities + Student Progress + Community.

वेबसाइटचे मुख्य उद्दिष्ट\:

- प्रत्येक विद्यार्थ्याची स्वतंत्र प्रोफाइल आणि डॅशबोर्ड.
- विद्यार्थ्यांना स्वतःचा प्रोग्रेस अपडेट करता येणे.
- कोऑर्डिनेटर आणि ॲडमिन यांना संपूर्ण कम्युनिटी मॅनेज करता येणे.
- इंटर्नशिप आणि इतर संधी मॅन्युअली पोस्ट करता येणे.
- प्रत्येक विद्यार्थ्याचा आणि संपूर्ण कॉलेजचा प्रोग्रेस रिपोर्ट पाहता येणे.
- Google Forms आणि Excel वर अवलंबून न राहता सर्व डेटा एका ठिकाणी ठेवणे.
